body:
| | | |
---
Good evening. Tonight is deadline night, and tomorrow my team will meet to discuss our fundraising numbers, which has a direct impact on our budget. It’s critical that we show that we have the resources to run a competitive campaign. New York is an expensive state to run in — and our opponent, Mike Lawler, has a big leg up over us in terms of money. But forget about that for a moment. I want to talk about why I’m in this race to begin with. I was a junior in high school on 9/11 when the Twin Towers fell. The next day, I began my West Point application. After graduating, I did six overseas deployments serving in combat zones like Iraq and Afghanistan. I did that out of a love for this country. Back then, I never thought that the greatest threat to America’s future would come from within our own borders. But the people running this administration do not share our values – or the values of the generations of Americans who fought and sacrificed to make this country better. **So I made the decision to run for Congress, again, out of love for this country.** My opponent, Mike Lawler, has become a rubber stamp for Trump and the MAGA agenda. Our campaign has a clear path to beating him and flipping this seat. But it’s going to be a tough fight. So please. [I am respectfully asking you to donate $10 or even $17 before midnight tonight. The only way we’ll be able to fire Lawler and take back the House is with your help. body:
This goes far beyond politics. The fabric of America is unweaving. | | | | | A Personal Message From Mike
---
Friend,
---
I am reaching out to you directly because, quite frankly, I don't know where else to turn. I've spent the last few hours pacing the room, trying to process what is happening. The latest developments are incredibly daunting, and my heart is heavy with an overwhelming sense of urgency.
---

**It is reality.** ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=200d0bb1f2184ed0a6b907932679e9c2&_e=275K1ypUWZAhSOPybBeQBFLNFv2JwltcDfMz60hWCXNGQGEY5gZtF8X3U4tLlAZlOWu2U8nA8iEANdq-4PurAhZFUlxYYgQdF3diqxmEL3n7fddZJG1KOYhJSzgE3vpZZENRK_K8ITl6xXwJ6dkcUXJTLv7kbiELZ41rViQyk7gvRXzf71tcCZyrLeGnD0VaESxSnt2ILcEPs3JZOiCOIQtAVBHPounegoGaHdhEDaczBiS_EeaeiFobtJ12oNLl1Wp_DSKRIgzI0xXhslsxbJzilq3PgpjQ19aahgWg0ttgo2nGkx4lEvK2iWrTCgjwiSEs6rzuv9pexE9bfg1zjfbdDRxPdgRyBoB5tLNbwRkpdrHqTzQaN1L9Q8SjfU5iNTo1XlDGOn2aJE9tnG0JpVPRoDMQCsRSBJ7Umd4UzE-GkH8Eanj2wk40EFIhkLxx5qcfe6N3LQv5tn9sX4nnzDBHSJwD7X0Bw3n16cBJamScpANTEmpNgFyTzfupugDT4OFINqsqiNjp42eSoRixl25HmqFvVaBQ9aDYR9Qlb15q9eBQz2eIEZhsnLUoZdDIvTuGvOscHC6H0vzIMmJEyWjoIVhEZJLHCsJyhsRv-eR_ZkwdRBBjvMT6Hd2cLXMffVMUEGtn7OdCj_C98arllWKt_PkrlbB30HMYBw2atlhzTVmioDz7bGulpyXH6M9Yb8mdjHBlbo12EF5utevOAwK49SQ-JGOvVAjBm1mIdS8GtTKtV551j7c4vLxkvQmu3DkbYzQUtMxc6ytUIOI5wXbNJcXRulU2uGg_HEHYUwA%3D)

Now we must win again. And we will win again.
Just like last time, I can’t do it alone.

subject: Checking back in
body:
Hi there, I appreciate you opening this message.
I’m reaching out one last time today because our July end-of-month deadline is just a few hours away at midnight.
I just checked in with my finance team, and we are still falling short of the budget target we set for tonight.
I'm not going to beat around the bush: The NRCC is watching our numbers closely. When you represent a seat that was decided by less than a thousand votes, every benchmark is a public test of our campaign’s strength.
National Republicans are counting on a mid-summer slowdown. They want nothing more than to see us miss our target so they can declare CA-45 vulnerable and flood our community with more outside money.

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Gregg Hull - Unfiltered
body:
His plans for New Mexico and his TIGHT race against Haaland | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/qyuoQ3RoBxQ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | New Mexico put a 15-year-old boy in a car, drove him to El Paso, and told him to walk across the bridge into Mexico by himself.

So who signed off on that?

That's the first thing we asked **Gregg Hull** on Wednesday. He was mayor of Rio Rancho for 12 years and he's the Republican running for governor against Deb Haaland.

**We had him for**[**a full hour**](https://us.list-manage.com/T8HlNEe0v_u?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)**and asked LOTS of important questions. He didn't dodge any of it**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/16fLZTGJXRo?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | **🚨 THE STATE WALKED A BOY TO THE MEXICAN BORDER AND LEFT HIM THERE**

CYFD is the agency that's supposed to protect New Mexico kids. They had custody of this one and drove him to the border anyway. Then Texas found him and called CYFD to hand him back.

What the agency said next is the part that set Gregg off, and you need to hear him read it out loud. He's asking for something now that nobody in Santa Fe is going to want to hand over.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/ntYV0R10B5J?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | **💰 HULL WANTS TO END THE STATE INCOME TAX. THAT'S $2.2 BILLION BACK TO US.**

Everybody in Santa Fe says you can't do that unless you raise some other tax to cover it. Gregg says that's wrong, and he works the numbers right there on the show. It comes down to the oil and gas money and one thing about a dollar that most people never think about.

And that $250 check the governor keeps talking about? Don't spend it yet. Mark explains why.

**🏛️ HE'S BEING OUTSPENT SEVEN TO ONE AND SAYS THE RACE IS TIED

** Haaland won her primary decisively and has significantly outraised Gregg so far. Mark pointed out that if this race stays competitive, it’s likely Gregg will face attacks from the other side. During the interview, Mark asked how Gregg plans to respond if and when that happens. Gregg laid out his strategy. Take a listen.
**🔥 WE ASKED HIM THE ABORTION QUESTION EVERYBODY EMAILS US ABOUT

** Can a governor end abortion in New Mexico? Krysty asked it flat out. His answer is honest, and plenty of people may not like it.

It also tells you exactly where to aim if you want this changed.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/57fGgsNDvke?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Some thoughts.
body:
Hi Peter, it’s
Gina. I know it’s late, but I wanted to reach out and share some thoughts
I’ve had on my mind.

We are officially less than 100 days away from Election Day.

In just 14 weeks, Texans will decide what kind of future we want for our
state — and there’s still so much work left to do.

Right now, our team is on the ground across Texas, organizing in
communities big and small, talking with voters, and building the
grassroots movement it will take to win this race.

But we can’t slow down now.

Taking on Greg Abbott and his corporate backers isn’t going to be easy. I
know that. I know they’ll spend whatever it takes to hold onto power.

But that’s why this moment matters.

Every conversation we have. Every volunteer we train. Every voter we
reach. Every dollar raised brings us one step closer to building the
campaign Texas deserves.

I know what this team is capable of when we come together. We’ve already
shown that this movement is powered by everyday Texans who believe our
state can be better.

So before you put your phone or computer away for the night, will you make
a contribution today to help us keep organizing, keep growing, and keep
fighting all the way to Election

– Gina

body:
How many politicians know what it’s like to be a regular Texan?

| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=1)
---
How many politicians know what it’s like to be a regular Texan? Grit is such a defining characteristic of Texan culture. In the past month or so, I’ve had my home’s AC unit replaced, plumbing repairs, and my beloved vehicle needed to be towed to the shop for major repairs... ha, oh, and a roofer is coming Monday. And I’m preparing to be back in the classroom Monday with my new first graders. Pushing through all of it, though, I find myself so grateful for the love, support, and resources to keep moving forward. I am humbled to know that too many Texans are struggling even more than my working family is. Thank you for sharing your stories and our campaign with people you know. Below, find upcoming events, hot topics, opportunities to help, and more! **_
Upcoming Events at a Glance_** _Next Saturday, August 8th_ | Kyle Market Day with [KBAD](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=gtygs8y15la-QqWnug14PNoDd0n4pCDy60p3H6wSXmf_nfQZ0LgAnZxW8E6XYUd_&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=2) \- Kyle-Buda Area Democrats will be at this adorable farmers and artisan market. Come say hi at the KBAD booth! _August 16th_ | Sign up for upcoming events like our [South Austin Meet & Greet](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/meet_greet_shady_hollow?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=3). Add your event to our calendar by emailing samantha@herdingcatscampaigns.com
---
**_Last Week's Highlights_** **__** ⏰ NEW POLL RESULTS: James Talarico is leading against Ken Paxton by 5 points! This is not a fluke. 53% of the respondents voted for Trump in 2024. **That means MAGA is losing support. And rapidly.** The opportunity to flip Texas is _very_ real, and we need to take advantage up and down the ballot. Like Talarico, I’m a teacher, so I’ve sat with parents when they tell me they lost their health insurance. Like Talarico, I’m fighting for universal healthcare and childcare so that Texas families can thrive. And like Talarico, I’m ready to take on my MAGA fanatic opponent who only cares about one thing: making Donald Trump happy. By investing in our TX-27 race, you are helping Democrats at all levels. We’re building the ground game to get voters to the polls. **_We have yard signs available!_** If you would like one and live in District 27, please fill out this [form](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/volunteer?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=4). We are making upgrades to our website. Everything you need to know before you vote: [Voter Info](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/voter_info?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=5) Please feel free to forward this newsletter to your network! And as always, thank you for being a part of this campaign. We are grateful for y'all's support!! To stay updated, please check out our socials—we appreciate the follows! [Instagram](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=mGkj6P31KIkRMZhtjQusDTV7GFpUpg6VLLUuif8PWjnWOC4lSKuv8GWqaLwO5DvX&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=6) [Facebook](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=gtygs8y15la-QqWnug14POmyE7cVjhGFcY_EAyuu8aYPN63MFjBoN881CO180NQWdZbpMYdzMIJrmMZDpBHNwA&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=7) [Website](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=8) If you’d like to make a contribution, please visit: [actblue.com](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn0XlvDo1X5NteDsJeOxzSIjywkdl8c2iNfTRzSvzGQb3Lve33NPnNz8OExPjAj5OKSkzhflpUG_7fanJMwvDnQJ&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_3&n=9). name: Tom Fitton
subject: FBI Projects 158-Year Wait for “Hidden Room” Records
body:
VA Removes 6,531 Noncitizens from Voter Rolls

[INSIDE JW]

FBI SAYS IT WILL TAKE 158 YEARS TO PROCESS “HIDDEN ROOM” RECORDS

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84518&L=38391&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS8zRVVVaEJEX1hXUT91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=ef23ebed76feb8862e5e727f5fd5ad2260f609d89f1e17be725911757895624d]

This is simply amazing. The FBI has told a federal court that, at a
rate of 500 pages a month, processing records from the “hidden
room” at FBI Headquarters would take approximately 158 years.

The room — now dubbed the “burn bag room” — holds over 2
million pages of records, according to the FBI’s own filing.
Then-Deputy Director Bongino said in May 2025 that some of the records
were found stashed “in bags.”

The figures came in a

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FOR ROBERT MUELLER RECORDS

The American people deserve a full accounting of Robert Mueller’s
record—from the FBI’s dramatic expansion of surveillance powers
after September 11 to the abusive special counsel investigation
targeting President Trump. The Justice Department should immediately
release every record concerning Mueller so Americans can judge his
work for themselves.

We sued in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia after
the Justice Department’s Office of Information Policy (OIP) failed
to respond to a March 24, 2026, FOIA request seeking:

> All records in any form related to the former FBI Director, Robert
> Swan Mueller, III, born on August 7, 1944, in New York City, NY, who
> died on March 20, 2026.

Mueller served as FBI director from September 2001 to September 2013.
During his tenure, the FBI significantly expanded its domestic
surveillance authorities. Among other powers, the bureau made
extensive use of expanded authorities under the USA PATRIOT Act of
2001, including National Security Letters
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84518&L=38318&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9vaWcuanVzdGljZS5nb3Yvc2l0ZXMvZGVmYXVsdC9maWxlcy9hcmNoaXZlL3NwZWNpYWwvczA3MDgvaW5kZXguaHRtP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=ea154cf38c1023edd6f9bd702d6ff6e9d52fbb93d98edbc677600922b0d08bb3],
which allowed the FBI to compel the production of financial,
telecommunications and internet records without prior judicial
approval while often prohibiting recipients from disclosing the
requests.

Three years after Mueller left the FBI, the bureau launched
“Crossfire Hurricane
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84518&L=38319&F=T&&hash=4f2bfc887b25297772cfd7a03cf30a721d2d9e1eac5943494937113789aed680
also known as “Russiagate,” into allegations of links between
Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign and Russia. Then-Deputy
Attorney General Rod Rosenstein appointed Mueller as special counsel
in May 2017 to continue the investigation. Mueller served in that role
until March 2019.

Mueller’s investigation concluded
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84518&L=38320&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3RoZS1tdWVsbGVyLXJlcG9ydC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=e1cc8f07ddbc5076d0e09dbe26444d947d9db90dc75a3f075c56a29aeb130a3e] that it
“did not establish that members of the Trump Campaign conspired or
coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference
activities.”

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84518&L=38321&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVzdGljZS5nb3YvYXJjaGl2ZXMvc2NvLWR1cmhhbS9tZWRpYS8xMzgxMjExL2RsP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=8310d7a05ea98578f8b2502873b05cea55be473d4c5abe81d926efe9a294ca12] that

A status conference is scheduled before U.S. District Judge Dabney L. Friedrich on August 3, 2026 in Washington, DC. Our 2025 complaint sought all records in the room, which it described as “[a]ll documents referenced by Deputy Director Dan Bongino” concerning a room at FBI Headquarters, as well as internal FBI communications among officials in the offices of Director Kash Patel and Deputy Director Bongino about the discovery of the documents, and any directives issued on how the records should be handled. VIRGINIA REMOVES 6,531 DECLARED NONCITIZEN REGISTRATIONS FROM VOTER ROLLS Records from the Virginia Department of Elections show the commonwealth cancelled 6,531 [] “declared noncitizen” voter registrations between June 2024 and June 2026 after we launched an inquiry. The Virginia Department of Elections produced records in response to the below June 2026 Judicial Watch request: Pursuant to Section 8(i) of the National Voter Registration Act (“NVRA [), Judicial Watch, Inc. respectfully requests from your office all pertinent records in the past two years concerning “the implementation of programs and activities conducted for the purpose of ensuring the accuracy and currency” of the Virginia official list of eligible voters. Specifically, Judicial Watch requests the following: 1. All records concerning the names and addresses of registrants removed from the official list of eligible voters pursuant to Va. Code Ann. § 24.2-427(B)(iii) and Va. Code Ann. § 24.2-427. 2. All records concerning all voter registrations that may not to be United States citizens by reason of reports from the Department of Motor Vehicles or from the Department of Elections based on information received from the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements Program (SAVE Program). 3. All ERIC reports, data, match lists, or other records received from or related to the Electronic Registration Information Center (ERIC) system concerning potential voter deaths, change-of-address notifications, or other eligibility issues (including any associated processing, verification, or removal actions taken by the Department of Elections in response to such ERIC reports). No voting histories were produced for the cancelled declared noncitizen registrations. According to an April 2026, Virginia Attorney General letter [ DMV [Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles] creates a list of “all persons who have indicated a noncitizen status” when applying for or renewing a license, or identification document. In practice, DMV compiles a list of any individual who checks “no” in response to the question “Are you a citizen?” in an online portal. There are reports that this method has resulted in flagging eligible citizens due to inadvertent user error. DMV furnishes this list of self-attested noncitizens to ELECT daily. ELECT then electronically matches the DMV list against the voter registration list, and transmits, for each match, information from the DMV list to the appropriate registrar. A stranger at the door doesn’t move the needle. If we want their vote, we’ve got to send someone they've seen before, someone who knows their name, someone who's already called, texted, or knocked on their door this month.
**[This is why Turning Point PAC's ballot-chasing model is built different.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NTV9AAwAAAAAAhQx7PgUnzIsyixZBHQg4E2t5f_G89hRER83YBC1_-d6xP5gO_SWtL0pyN2088cxuekcEG4lAkQk7VKwMOjvXSx6zr2AOVEniW3PaElL)**

Early voting starts in less than 8 weeks. And the margin of our House majority — the margin that protects everything President Trump has built — will be decided by whether our people show up or stay home.

That's a warning._ Because in the summer of 2026, the socialist left isn't hiding anymore. This past Tuesday, Republicans of Clark County went door-to-door promoting Republican politics and providing voters with resources on Republican 7th Congressional District candidates. **Taylor County**
With fair season peaking, Taylor County Republicans made sure to represent at the Taylor County Fair. **Waukesha County**
Waukesha County Republicans, hot off a two-week stretch over which they attended SIX parades, kept their pace high by simultaneously tabling at both the Waukesha County Fair from the 17th to the 19th and the Maxwell Street Days flea market on the 18th and 19th. In line with previous weeks, Waukesha GOP marched in the Dousman Derby Days parade on the 26th. Two days later, Tom Tiffany visited the county, joining members for a meet and greet. Great work! **Calumet County**
Calumet County had a great turnout for their monthly membership/conservative citizens meeting on July 27th in Chilton, where they heard from all four District 1 Senate candidates. **St. Croix County**
We handed out lots of yard signs, lit and voter guides, and had several guests, including State Rep. Rob Kreibich, Senator Rob Stafsholt, Nate Pollnow for Sec. of State, and CD7 Candidates at their county fair booth. They also hosted a Save Wisconsin Saturday to hit doors, write postcards, and hang signs! So far they have distributed about 500 yard signs and wrote over 2,000 postcards. **Sauk County**
Sauk County participated in the Plain, WI, Fire and EMS parade. **Washington County**
Washington County Republicans showcased a handmade quilt at their county fair booth this year and conducted a straw poll. | Friend,
We did something different in Wisconsin, and people are sitting up and taking notice. With a smaller budget than our Pennsylvania Supreme Court race in 2025, we couldn't run a full field and TV campaign. Traditional organizers. Mailers. Ads on every screen.
That wasn't in the cards.
So instead of doing less of what everyone else does, we did something no one else was doing.
Our co-founder Joe Bachman was interviewed by Wisconsin Public Radio about the cutting-edge voter contact technology we deployed in the state and how it helped us punch way above our weight:
---
| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001CLF3-nxU1nJKVIplhU8IqHtmv-ybY5mMJuUBFExxQh7gP8LXKmRGrNnTtYP9jZN7Ws0-N2ZxPgHLjO5MWVYmzOAK5HynS2D4M88KZq0TccGeOhMngecIghST4ABWubGRhSHVhkKymnZ-SUk-8-NDWXuwCH3VFApeJyo3ueayfkRWYoEEwUv-3j5Yia5NH0XJK7cf4diIBg9DTvigPKsUzd6Iq1CIBN-CbQFrTjaVAIretoz82_qi1czRw31A9aiaFVXFIjCivn4=&c=Uv9EtlbrGY4Ji7gdboASMKnxjH7oe4KiCwXklIGRpGIQDYQ5QXCrVA==&ch=eYUE38LIxomB6m56oqQuPCtOMITPJxJAdm2qxa80e2XRu33HWv3Ugg==)
---
| Here's the core idea: every Democrat deserves an organizer in their pocket.
An actual, interactive tool built specifically to talk a voter through exactly what they needed to know. Where to vote, what ID to bring, how the process works. One that could speak to Chris Taylor's record and positions on the issues. One that could answer questions with accurate information, at any hour, at a massive scale: we used it to reach over 1 million voters.
We share the concerns about AI's energy demands, economic disruption, and impact on workers. That’s why we worked with our partners at Convos to keep our footprint minimal. And for what it's worth: this approach has a smaller environmental impact than a large mailer campaign.
AI is becoming a bigger part of political campaigns. As we read stories about deepfakes and misinformation, Defend Our Courts is proud to lead the way in using this technology responsibly and transparently to have real conversations with the voters we need to reach. This also isn't about replacing the field organizers and volunteers who are the backbone of our democracy. It's about giving them a force multiplier. Reaching voters they couldn't reach. Having conversations that would otherwise never happen.
Wisconsin showed it can work and we couldn't have done it without you.
Tens of thousands of Democrats across the country pitched in to fuel this work. You made a difference in a race that far too few people were paying attention to.
Court races are like that. Under the radar. Underestimated. Until suddenly they're not. 2026 will have more high-stakes judicial races, with the same type of stakes as Wisconsin and Pennsylvania. **Good morning!** On this day in 1981, the cable network MTV launched with the Buggles' _Video Killed the Radio Star_ , aptly symbolizing the new visual era of music. [See MTV's first-day playlist](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkEtugzAURVcDs6Bn8zEMPIjSorZKqv7SqiP0wM_ByMQIO0Hsvkq7hI7u4ErnSOfr0BzQWHM-PeNIMmjXnGnxlkKguelxRI-nmcgHp4zHeWRsNNY2HHixgXIDrFFo7NpksZKaiFMak2SizHNRVjmPe6k0BwKhKgWapXnXFbrsBFQd41gAtrGRNxqUwBhAxSDJBFRaUYnUpoI4RRmQMsHNyeDMOfSk7equNCedG2Mr-xAmH6XbiNcRr5dlSVZ3CZeWbn_E68niao0PUVr_zd3L_r4bHmF7LD4Qr9tPMbwdWbt_n9phtz58P73u4lmqaTHWGl-IKIPTiMb--sK_Il0l_wkAAP__eLx61Q).

Many thanks to the hundreds of readers who responded to our question about owning a dog, and thanks especially to those of you sent in photos of your pet. We have to say that they were all beautiful, and we very much enjoyed seeing them. And don't worry cat lovers, your turn is coming! Are you paying $139 a year for Amazon Prime just to get free shipping? Odds are you're only using a fraction of what that money buys. Peter,
The Mouth of Sauron, Karoline Leavitt, has spoken: Donald Trump's "patience is running out" with Senate Majority Leader John Thune on his inability to force through Trump's voter suppression bill the SAVE Act.
But Thune seems to also be losing patience, which is either a very good sign or a signal that Trump will threaten his position as Majority Leader next to get what he wants.
Thune fired back at Trump in a veiled comment aimed at Leavitt:
"Well maybe she or somebody else ought to get on the phone and get the votes, right?" Thune told reporters. "It's 50 around here. And, so, instead of pointing the finger at Republicans, they might think about going after the people who are stopping it on the floor, which is the Democrats."

Defend Our Courts is fighting to elect independent-minded judges on state courts that will put the people and the law above Donald Trump.
We helped save the Democratic majority on the PA supreme court last year by working to reelect three Democratic justices up for retention. But more importantly, each of those justices were steadfastly committed to the rule of law, democracy, and to free and fair elections.
There are almost zero GOP or right-leaning candidates in judicial races anywhere in the country who are willing to speak the truth about Trump's 2020 election lies.

## Second Poll Shows Tight Senate Race
A new [Fox News poll](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAURp8GOwwgzGhBsY3dv-2W5gpXvQkjRG5G5-03ziv89UnOl-_8-5l-gBLt6194oedrydOOZ03IjMfEkOCgkBNCpH0tcHHeOZcyGWUeUvVS6SkCpc9km-hnFQfdoNfP3rne6KdtNj9bq8BErQJo16ObwxwGM_QOhs457Bryt0z1SmutjDNteMxRB4Wz7QbjuiCswkicj5Y3ZLygLumT33i0Ib-a5DfmUkX3R5hRmPE8z3bJ1_3i5sKMJSdiClWYccmXvIksOSW55iIjvalS3qusGxSUX7-suAOjPCBgc_hYTkqJ6uMprFpfQOm7zL_r9fbmfwAAAP__sd2COg) of Texas registered voters shows Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 51% to 48% in the U.S. Senate race. The 3-point gap sits inside the margin of error. It's the second poll in a week to show Talarico ahead, after Texas Public Opinion Research put him up 45% to 40% Tuesday. Talarico draws 68% of independents and 98% of Democrats, while 89% of Republicans back Paxton. About one in four non-MAGA Republicans said they'd vote for Talarico. Nearly 4 in 10 voters named inflation as the top issue in their Senate vote, and 2 in 10 named immigration. Texas hasn't [sent a Democrat to the Senate](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ygzAQhJ9GdGIkIX5cqEhD57QpmUM6jDJniYGzwW-fwZk8Qfqdb_fbr-twhUgx3T7hjo6PKQ8J942QGdeBgWCNPhNCiOm2wME5cV6WwSjTSNVJpYcAkV6DLYIbVbjoAp1uu7rujG5tMTsYNZp2BK_8pLvKogdV-fECXfAq2LqI7oSpTmmtlalN6ZsxaK9wtNXF1JUXVmGInNeSZ2Q8YJvolZ-4lj7fC3Iz87KJ6kOYXph-3_dyyodp5vzYOKczJEyPhJ5jTsL0f1by10dumIBRruBRvvFyyUTy-0EveU4rVheWPRLFrWmFVbc7RHp38_8eezrzEwAA__87IILS) since 1988.
## Weekend Front Nudges the Heat Down
A [weak summer cold front](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOnDAQBOCnMZ3R2piDK1ykofvTpkSLvYB1xkZmOe7ePiKvkHo0n0bz52f8wRBDWn7jRpY_cx4TXUckZiojY8QSXI6EPqRlxw_nxHnfRw36IaGXoEaPIX5HU3k7gX-qiqzq-rbttepMtVoyfTtNzrgOnn3TkgfjJkT0vjdmBlUFe2PQg1IKdKtr95i8ckCTaZ66bZwwQD5wLjWvxPTBY47f_KZSu7xV0a7M-yGaX0IPQg_XddUvLnSHQg-3LfQAndBDA0IPx7ltVKTL0cuUWa6Z5VxyYnmFGOVUCF_y3OVKyPIiuRDLLSdeJZ7LebA8k6dy4VfooSrW73ctHI9OGFg2DPHfKv6_L99W_w0AAP__8A2JuQ) will slide into North, Northeast, and East Texas this weekend, dropping highs from the upper 90s into the lower 90s by Sunday. The heat dome that has run the state all week is shifting west toward Arizona, Nevada, and California, opening the door for northerly winds on its eastern edge. East Texas counties sat under heat advisories through Friday evening with heat indices near 105 degrees. Behind the front, morning lows should fall into the lower 70s, with a few upper 60s early next week. Houston gets less of a break. Forecasters there expect highs [near 100 today](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OozAUhZ_GdEb2xfwVLrahy7ZbImPfwFUMRuYmJG-_YmbeYNqj7_zo_LuNN0eRtvmvW9Hy-57GDc8jIjPmkV10mXyK6AJt8-7enDZO-z6CgkaqTio9BkfxM5oi2EmFXhdoddvVdQe6NcVipwZ6h7rWxt1N13dt0FhPvvLT1GvTQkH2ClOd0lorqKH0zRS0VziZqoe68sIoDMQpl7wg49sd9_hJL8ylT2sR7cK8H6L6I2AQMJznWfpI_gFLeh6ctou6dHS8YBYwXHUCBtUKGColYAhumzGn5yEXdCznTPshf9zyJF4kZ9ojykAz8TcU0ooyJv_AIGkTMBTZhv2kGOloWmHUvDqKXwv5d7--LPwPAAD__1Krjcs) and upper 90s next week, with overnight lows close to 80.
## Texas' Top Private Company Isn't H-E-B
Austin telecom company Purple Communications ranked as [Texas' highest entry](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3O4yAQheGrwZ0tGPxbUGzjLttuaQ0wiZEwIDOJk7tfZaW9gq9_dI70_rltNwwxpMdvPMjw-563RFeNxEznxhjxDC5HQh_So-Cbc-JcygYSxlbOrVSbxxA_W994Y6VfVENGTfMwzKCmvtkN2tmp3lqpldVae_STW0Z1JzUqB8PSBPMdk7NUSkkYoHOj9cpJsr1eYNBO9JJ84Hx2vBPTG-s9fvKLzs7lo4lmZy5V6F8CVgHrdV3d8amYMHFOIX-RgNU-a0hUq4AVTw4ukoB1J9vapyOqraXK7X9EtQXQI8Aiu7KX5jS-XCHGUMdJ9PJxYIj_zvlnyV4G_gYAAP__vCOBwQ) on _Time_ 's first list of America's 500 best private companies, landing at No. 56. Purple provides video relay, interpreting, and real-time translation for deaf and hard-of-hearing customers. Its score of 88.72 put it 19 spots ahead of H-E-B, the San Antonio grocer that usually tops Texas rankings. _Time_ built the [ranking with Statista](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OrDAQhE9jMkZ2YzAEDl5CNi_dEDV2z0xLBiO7NT-3X7HaG2xSyaeqT6qv63JFTrzf_-NGXt63vOz0qolEqCyCCQuHnAgj7_cD35J3ycexgIah1WOrzRKR02exTfSrjpNpyBs39v0Ixtnm4Z2eYIxgDQ7TOE3BQe-0sauN8TZR5xr255getTFGQw-XMKzRBE2r7Sbou6CspsiSy0UeJPTGekuf_KRyCXlrkn-IHFV1_xTMCmbhjU6gYMYiHBIpmE-Dglm7M8YTbVQ4YG1XqtIehZ8o1Ia8Hbgz1fa30BQfjxenxHVwyur7hpx-tPK3s54evgMAAP__EwJ7yQ), scoring companies on employee satisfaction surveys, plus net benefit on society, knowledge, health, and the environment. East Texas counties sat under heat advisories through Friday evening with heat indices near 105 degrees. Behind the front, morning lows should fall into the lower 70s, with a few upper 60s early next week. Houston gets less of a break. subject: The Washington Post
body:
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1317?t=1&akid=980%2E3892029%2EBC4qW7)

Peter: Exactly six years ago, I retired from active military service.
I had no intention to resign from a career I loved, having served for more than 21 years in uniform. But it became clear that Donald Trump had a vendetta against me, and that he would do everything in his power to punish me for speaking truth to power.
On that first day of retirement, I wrote an article in _The Washington Post_ discussing the need to have public servants with the moral courage to protect our democracy. This is more relevant than ever.
I’ve attached the op-ed below. Thank you for taking a few minutes to read it.

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260801-1&refcode2=980_3892029_BC4qW7&akid=980%2E3892029%2EBC4qW7)
After 21 years, six months and 10 days of active military service, I am now a civilian. I made the difficult decision to retire because a campaign of bullying, intimidation and retaliation by President Trump and his allies forever limited the progression of my military career.
This experience has been painful, but I am not alone in this ignominious fate. The circumstances of my departure might have been more public, yet they are little different from those of dozens of other lifelong public servants who have left this administration with their integrity intact but their careers irreparably harmed.
A year ago, having served the nation in uniform in positions of critical importance, I was on the cusp of a career-topping promotion to colonel. A year ago, unknown to me, my concerns over the president’s conduct and the president’s efforts to undermine the very foundations of our democracy were precipitating tremors that would ultimately shake loose the facade of good governance and publicly expose the corruption of the Trump administration.
At no point in my career or life have I felt our nation’s values under greater threat and in more peril than at this moment. Our national government during the past few years has been more reminiscent of the authoritarian regime my family fled more than 40 years ago than the country I have devoted my life to serving.
Our citizens are being subjected to the same kinds of attacks tyrants launch against their critics and political opponents. Those who choose loyalty to American values and allegiance to the Constitution over devotion to a mendacious president and his enablers are punished. The president recklessly downplayed the threat of the pandemic even as it swept through our country. The economic collapse that followed highlighted the growing income disparities in our society. Millions are grieving the loss of loved ones and many more have lost their livelihoods while the president publicly bemoans his approval ratings.
There is another way.
During my testimony in the House impeachment inquiry, I reassured my father, who experienced Soviet authoritarianism firsthand, saying, “Do not worry, I will be fine for telling the truth.” Despite Trump’s retaliation, I stand by that conviction. Even as I experience the low of ending my military career, I have also experienced the loving support of tens of thousands of Americans. Theirs is a chorus of hope that drowns out the spurious attacks of a disreputable man and his sycophants.
Since the struggle for our nation’s independence, America has been a union of purpose: a union born from the belief that although each individual is the pilot of their own destiny, when we come together, we change the world. We are stronger as a woven rope than as unbound threads.
America has thrived because citizens have been willing to contribute their voices and shed their blood to challenge injustice and protect the nation. It is in keeping with that history of service that, at this moment, I feel the burden to advocate for my values and an enormous urgency to act.
Despite some personal turmoil, I remain hopeful for the future for both my family and for our nation. Impeachment exposed Trump’s corruption, but the confluence of a pandemic, a financial crisis and the stoking of societal divisions has roused the soul of the American people. A groundswell is building that will issue a mandate to reject hate and bigotry and a return to the ideals that set the United States apart from the rest of the world. I look forward to contributing to that effort.
In retirement from the Army, I will continue to defend my nation. I will demand accountability of our leadership and call for leaders of moral courage and public servants of integrity. I will speak about the attacks on our national security. I will advocate for policies and strategies that will keep our nation safe and strong against internal and external threats. I will promote public service and exalt the contribution that service brings to all areas of society.
The 23-year-old me who was commissioned in December 1998 could never have imagined the opportunities and experiences I have had. I joined the military to serve the country that sheltered my family’s escape from authoritarianism, and yet the privilege has been all mine.
When I was asked why I had the confidence to tell my father not to worry about my testimony, my response was, “Congressman, because this is America. This is the country I have served and defended, that all my brothers have served, and here, right matters.”
To this day, despite everything that has happened, I continue to believe in the American Dream. I believe that in America, right matters. I want to help ensure that right matters for all Americans.

It wasn’t long ago when a Democrat represented Florida in the Senate. As a former combat veteran and national security expert who has stood up to Trump, Alex has the background to win back voters and flip this seat.
If everyone reading this email donated just $15 to Alex’s campaign, we could have the resources to share our message with undecided voters and win this race.

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Introducing the Mississippi Wire
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/july4th-12854287?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Something has been quietly disappearing from Mississippi life over the past couple of decades, almost unnoticed.

Local newsrooms have been cutting back, not because they want to, but because they have had to. Advertising moved to the internet, papers shrank, reporters had to do more with less, and some things were no longer covered.

So school boards now can make decisions few parents get to hear about. A county signs away a third of the property taxes on a new plant, and it appears in no headline. Someone stands up at a council meeting and makes the single most important point anyone will make about that city's finances all year — and makes it to a half-empty room.

And yet paradoxically, there is no shortage of what we call news. There is more of it than ever. But look closely at where it comes from. The newspaper writes up what the television station covered. The television station covers what the radio was talking about. The radio talks about what was in the newspaper. It is an echo chamber — a great deal of noise, not always much signal.

That gap is what the Mississippi Wire exists to fill. Click on the image below to read it.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/r6ZgjfJca1O?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
| The Mississippi Wire is more of a news service than a commentary. It's not there to tell you what we make of somebody else's reporting. The Wire aims to give you stories that have simply not appeared anywhere before.

Here is some of what the Mississippi Wire published this week:
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| These are the ordinary decisions that determine what your children are taught and what your property is taxed at — and until now, most of them happened without anybody outside the room knowing they had happened at all.

We have only been going a couple of weeks, and the traction has been real - more readers, faster, than we expected, and a steady stream of people telling us they had no idea any of this was going on where they live.

Have a look for yourself at [M](https://us.list-manage.com/V__w_uno2el?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)[ississippiWire.News](https://us.list-manage.com/HOhBM0DJjlA?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3). And if you find a story there that your neighbor ought to see, send it to them. That is how a state gets its local news back.
---
| [Forward this email to a friend!](https://us.list-manage.com/nOZcCIVq9u1?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3 "Forward this email to a friend!")
---
| |
---
Warm regards,

Douglas Carswell
President & CEO
Mississippi Center for Public Policy

|
---

Peter, democracy only works when people participate. And in just **three days** , voters will head to the polls to make their voice heard in our Primary Election.

But before voting officially begins, we want to know: _are you prepared?_

If you haven't already, now is the time to make your plan to vote. Take a few minutes to go through our voter checklist to make sure you've covered all the basics — from confirming your registration and polling location to checking your voting options and knowing what to bring on Election Day.
**Voter Checklist:**

☐**Confirm you're registered to vote.** Make sure your registration is active and your information is up to date.

☐******Know your voting plan.** Decide whether you'll vote early, by mail (if available), or on Election Day.

☐ **Find your polling place.** Don't wait until the last minute — know exactly where you'll vote.

☐ **Check what ID you need.** Review your state's voter ID requirements before heading to the polls.

☐**Mark Election Day on your calendar.** Set a reminder so you don't forget.

☐ **Bring a friend or family member.** Voting together helps strengthen turnout.
A few minutes of preparation now can make all the difference when it's time to cast your ballot.

* * *
Peter, This is the last**full month** of our campaign before the primary election. We’ve got a lot of exciting plans ahead of us, such as house parties, canvassing days, and community events. body:
A review of Vikram's July posts...

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mansharamani/vikram-update-july-2026?e=93b2c2b824)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/b0E4HPVjwAb?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
| | | | | |
# Mansharamani Musings
---
| | [](https://us.list-manage.com/tZ8xj_A1WEL?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)During July, I spoke with leaders from various industries and across many geographies. The five biggest topics of interest I encountered in July were (1) geopolitics and the Iran War...but with increasing curiosity about the future of Cuba, (2) how the new round of tariffs and energy price volatility will impact the outlook for inflation and the Fed’s response, (3) whether artificial intelligence infrastructure was a bubble about to burst, (4) Chinese economic weakness and whether it was driven by lower energy usage during the second quarter, and (5) how the increasing commercialization of space will impact sectors on earth. Best wishes for a thought-filled August!_**
- Vikram**_

---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Y6dFIku3ukW?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
| | **JULY 4, 2026**

Inspired by my attendance at a naturalization ceremony in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, two years ago, I have been writing about America each year around Independence Day. Spending the day of America’s birth with her newest citizens, it was impossible for me not to think about my own family’s immigrant journey, and each year I pause and reflect with gratitude about our great nation.

Last year, in “[Still a Shining City on a Hill](https://us.list-manage.com/v4NUAzI4r0I?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586),” I wrote about my family’s journey, in particular that of my father, who traveled from India to Africa to a little apartment in Queens to the life he built in New Jersey. This year, as America turns 250, I suspect it will not surprise readers to learn that I am as convinced as ever that the United States is still the greatest nation on Earth. Despite political headlines and polarized dogma, America is still shining. More so than ever, actually...

---
| [CLICK HERE TO CONTINUE READING](https://us.list-manage.com/OOglQl2o_cw?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/IpVkAk5hNat?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
| | **July 12, 2026**

I have spent a career arguing that the most important signals rarely announce themselves. The skyscraper that tops out at the market peak. The pizza order that spikes in the Pentagon parking lot the night before a military operation. The private-label, single-serve trade-down in the frozen aisle that telegraphs a stressed consumer months before the macro data confirm it. Connecting seemingly irrelevant dots is not a parlor trick. It is, I’d argue, the only reliable way to see around corners and navigate uncertainty.
And the latest dot that has caught my eye is the size of a poppy seed that no one on Wall Street is watching: **a tick that is quietly building a short position in animal protein.** At the root of the development is a disease the tick spreads. It’s a condition called [alpha-gal syndrome](https://us.list-manage.com/5CbkOTaZZyr?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), or AGS, for short. It is an allergy (often severe, sometimes fatal) — to a sugar present in almost every non-primate mammal. AGS essentially makes you allergic to meat...
---
| [CLICK HERE TO CONTINUE READING](https://us.list-manage.com/UWFOImScC3m?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/fS1FzodiFz8?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
| | **July 19, 2026**

The World Cup final is later today (Argentina and the legendary Messi versus Spain and Lamine Yamal) at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey—and I’ll be watching. My son is an avid soccer fan and watching the games together has been one of those family moments you don’t plan but never forget. Sitting on the couch, cheering for the home team (or the favorite...or the underdog...), groaning at bad calls, high-fiving after goals, with the most important people in my world. And of course, how could we not fall in love with the Norwegian viking row...

As I watched the games this year, I was reminded of Franklin Foer’s book [_How Soccer Explains the World_](https://us.list-manage.com/tZdiSpHqvt2?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) , which came out in 2004 and used soccer as a lens to explain tribalism, nationalism, corruption, and the enduring power of identity. It was a contrarian book during an era when Thomas Friedman’s [_The World Is Flat_](https://us.list-manage.com/ynQ0uCWz9eP?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) (2005) was on everyone’s mind, when globalization was supposed to sand down every rough edge and turn the world into one big market. Who could forget his famous thesis that no two countries that had a McDonald’s had ever gone to war with each other?
Foer pushed back. His argument was that the Beautiful Game revealed something uglier underneath. Foer suggested that tribalism doesn’t dissolve with free trade but rather deepens. Familiarity breeds contempt, as the old saying goes...
---
| [CLICK HERE TO CONTINUE READING](https://us.list-manage.com/VSLjnEH_toJ?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1pHQRH9e3wX?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
| | **JULY 26, 2026**

As many of you are aware, I run a frozen pizza factory. Pepperoni pizza is one of our best sellers, so it should not be surprising that I spend a lot of time thinking about pork prices. And while the price of your pizza is obviously impacted by the price of pepperoni on top of it, you may find it interesting that the price is increasingly being set in Beijing, not in Iowa or North Carolina.
How’s that? Well, it turns out that the Middle Kingdom is the world’s largest consumer of pork. China consumes [57 million metric tons of pork per year](https://us.list-manage.com/bMMoHe0gYHh?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)—roughly **half of all the pork eaten on Earth**. And pork in China isn’t like chicken in America. The Chinese character for “home” (家) is literally a pig under a roof and pork is deeply intertwined with Chinese culture. So when anything disrupts China’s pork supply (such as a disease, tariff, or trade war), shockwaves flow through global markets. Including, eventually, to the pepperoni we put on pizzas in America....

body:
The flag belongs to all of us. Patriotism belongs to all of us. This country is ours, just as much as it is Donald Trump’s or any of his MAGA die-hards.
#
Peter:
20 years ago, VoteVets started as a scrappy organization founded by a few pissed off Veterans who were ready to fight back against the Republican Party.
Today, it’s a nationwide organization composed of millions of Veterans, members of Military Families, professionals from intelligence and national security... and, frankly, a ton of regular people who understand what we’re trying to do here.
This isn’t your run-of-the-mill Democratic political shop. We’re not afraid to talk about war, about foreign policy, about what it means to fight for your country abroad and then come home to do the same thing. We go places most other organizations won’t, speak to people they can’t, and we win when nobody else can.
The flag belongs to all of us. Patriotism belongs to all of us. This country is ours, just as much as it is Donald Trump’s or any of his MAGA die-hards. And more than that, we actually believe in it. We believe in our democracy, our Constitution, our way of life — and we swore an oath to support and defend it.
That’s our mission, that’s what VoteVets is about and what sets us apart. And as we push forward to the elections in November, we’re asking you to double down on your past support and recommit to our mission.
[**If you are with VoteVets, if you believe what we do matters, and you’re willing to stand with us in the fight for our country, add your name and personally endorse the VoteVets mission.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/Aug_VV_mission_em/?source=em260801-1-120&refcode2=35415.3013755.8ASNxI&akid=35415%2E3013755%2E8ASNxI)

Peter Willis,

We have ONE WEEKEND left until Michigan’s primary next Tuesday, and we are
up against one of the biggest corporate onslaughts we’ve EVER faced in our
push to power Abdul El-Sayed to victory.

AIPAC was just exposed for dropping a jaw-dropping $30 million to defeat
Abdul – more than they have EVER spent to buy a seat in Congress.

the biggest test of its influence yet

While Abdul’s AIPAC-backed opponent, Haley Stevens, cozies up to
billionaires and cuts deals behind closed doors, Abdul is fighting for all
of us. So Our Revolution has deployed our organizers to Michigan to fight
back against the super PACs, billionaires, and TV attack ads by having
REAL conversations with voters across the state.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37963?t=1057&amount=22&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&refcode=email-20260801nd&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=11142%2E5885482%2EvtC68q ]We have ONE WEEKEND left and every hour counts — and every door knocked,
every phone call made matters. If enough of us chip in $25 today, we can
turbo-charge our ground game and power Abdul to victory. Will you rush a
donation now to help?

If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37964?source=email-20260801&t=1060&akid=11142%2E5885482%2EvtC68q ]Photo of Abdul speaking at a rally

Abdul is the real deal. He’s proposed a 7% wealth tax on billionaires’
fortunes to fund health care, schools, and more. While millions face
skyrocketing health care costs with no help in sight, Abdul remains
steadfast in his commitment to winning Medicare for All.

That’s why AIPAC, Fox News, the Democratic establishment, and MAGA have
all teamed up to try to stop him. Meanwhile, we’re relying on thousands of
small-dollar donations and local organizers.

Right now, Abdul has the edge. But 14% of voters have still not made up
their minds and some polls are finding Stevens is ahead. Meanwhile, the
dark money ads against him are COVERING the airwaves.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37964?source=email-20260801&t=1061&akid=11142%2E5885482%2EvtC68q ]Headline: El-Sayed has the edge as Michigan’s Senate primary nears

WEEKEND, every dollar recruits volunteers, sends texts, and helps us knock
on doors — voter by voter, block by block.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37963?t=1054&amount=22&refcode=email-20260801nd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=11142%2E5885482%2EvtC68q ]If enough of us donate $25 today, we’ll have what we need to turbo-charge
our voter outreach across Michigan in the final crucial days before the
August 4 primary and beyond. Are you in?

This primary isn't just about one candidate. It’s about sending a message:
Michigan’s future can’t be bought. If Abdul wins, it will be thanks to
people like you who stepped up when it mattered most.

We know what we’re up against. But with your support, we know we can win.

When we organize, we win.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Inside Foxconn’s massive new facility in Houston, cameras captured NVIDIA’s CEO standing shoulder-to-shoulder with humanoid robots. Real machines — walking, turning, and working on the floor of what will become America’s first large-scale humanoid production line.

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. | | Hey there Peter, it’s Kathleen Riebe. Utah is like nowhere else in the world. From the Wasatch Mountains that tower over us to the striking red rocks in the ‘Mighty 5’ that inspire us, there’s so much about our state to be thankful for. But when people ask me why I love Utah so much, there’s only one answer I can give: Our sense of community. It’s what brought me to public service, and it’s what helped me decide to enter this race for Congress to represent Utah’s first district. [_**In just a moment, I’m going to tell you more about why uplifting this community in Washington is so important to me. But first, I need your help. This campaign is powered entirely by individuals who want what’s best for Utah, not corporate PACs or special interests. I need a strong network of grassroots supporters by my side if we’re going to win in November. I’ve been an educator for almost 25 years, Peter. I stepped into the classroom for the first time on September 11, 2001. My heart was breaking for our country, but I felt a profound sense of purpose as I spoke with my students about what it means to serve our community in times of crisis.
In the classroom, you learn quickly what kinds of problems a community is struggling with. Everything from economic insecurity and rising health care costs to divisive culture wars eventually walks through the schoolhouse doors.
**Supporting my students through those struggles is exactly what inspired me to run for the State Board of Education and later the State Senate.**
I’ve spent years cutting through the political theatrics in Salt Lake City to deliver real results for working families. Now, I’m ready to take that same fight to Washington.
This campaign is building a movement of hardworking Utahns who believe that “public service” should actually be about service, not petty power grabs. That’s why I’m refusing to take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Peter, this is our moment to restore common sense and integrity to our representation, but I can’t do it without your help.

clean_body: | | | Hey there Peter, it’s Kathleen Riebe. Utah is like nowhere else in the world. From the Wasatch Mountains that tower over us to the striking red rocks in the ‘Mighty 5’ that inspire us, there’s so much about our state to be thankful for. But when people ask me why I love Utah so much, there’s only one answer I can give: Our sense of community. It’s what brought me to public service, and it’s what helped me decide to enter this race for Congress to represent Utah’s first district. = | = I’ve been an educator for almost 25 years, Peter. I stepped into the classroom for the first time on September 11, 2001. My heart was breaking for our country, but I felt a profound sense of purpose as I spoke with my students about what it means to serve our community in times of crisis. In the classroom, you learn quickly what kinds of problems a community is struggling with. Everything from economic insecurity and rising health care costs to divisive culture wars eventually walks through the schoolhouse doors. Supporting my students through those struggles is exactly what inspired me to run for the State Board of Education and later the State Senate. I’ve spent years cutting through the political theatrics in Salt Lake City to deliver real results for working families. Now, I’m ready to take that same fight to Washington. This campaign is building a movement of hardworking Utahns who believe that “public service” should actually be about service, not petty power grabs. That’s why I’m refusing to take a dime of corporate PAC money. Peter, this is our moment to restore common sense and integrity to our representation, but I can’t do it without your help. = | = = | = = | = = I’m so grateful to have you on this team. | | Dear Friend, Here’s a thought-provoking video from Hillsdale College for you today. It’s a powerful lesson from our free online course, “C.S. Lewis on Christianity,” focused on one of life’s most important questions: **Why do we experience guilt—and what does it mean?** **Watch your free video here for the answer, according to the greatest apologist of the 20 th century:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/cs-lewis-christianity-free-lesson](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyU0c1unDAUxfGnMTuQsc1HFiwqEZKozdBE02ZpeewLXMnYiGsyyttXqTIPkPVf-i3OeXvWzwY9hvlkVuiQSLvo9HX5cPEKE4CfD_RJCy7qnLc5L7WxCd9BK5O5rhJlO7UZdGXTVtWd5KrOlq5qjKqrRti6NLKp7spmupj2ouDSSOvklGH36fGWl6XiiqtiklIJdZGc27LiRjDFj82ZBAUGQgdkY9y26DGhpSLuc-a7JaWNmPzBxMDEgGGKxYLekzMeCnAHE4Ol3MMVKbfLjpTQBEwf-bQD5B6IYmByIMtkzzlv6xMXSjwNYz_29_cvTNRHWrU162ZwDkz2lv5j-pf8ahSP3QKT_bZH2sAmDPNXWsHhsTLZw2rQ36wYEoTEZH9-HP88PJ5_v45_x59Ppwf90uRv59f8Nku2d267ovdIdcMUnz-VwsY1S9_86L0T_wIAAP__tlydeA) C.S. Lewis believed that our universal sense of right and wrong points to something real—an objective moral law, and a moral lawgiver behind it. But he didn’t stop there. Lewis also explains that true Christian conversion follows a pattern: first, a kind of death to our old life... and then a rising to something higher than before. It’s a difficult idea, but also a hopeful one. subject: Trump always needs someone to blame
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Trump would rather settle political scores than do the job he was elected to do.
#
Did you see this, Peter?
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260801-1.hkVc6F&amount=5&refcode=em20260801-921&t=2&akid=921%2E34582%2EdN8FMz)
This week, cyberattacks targeted local water systems in multiple states across the nation, and federal authorities are investigating whether Iran was responsible.
**Donald Trump’s response? Blame me and the people of Minnesota — without a shred of evidence.**
Without even mentioning the other six impacted states, Trump claimed: _“I think that Minnesota is behind it. You know who is behind it? Minnesota. Because they’re grossly incompetent. I think the governor is behind it. I don’t think there was an Iranian cyberattack. I think that Minnesota ought to get its act together.”_
Trump can’t beat Iran because he’s too busy waging war with Minnesota. His obsession with our state truly knows no bounds.
This is what he does. When something goes wrong, he looks for someone to blame. When people stand up to him, he tries to intimidate them. And instead of doing the job he was elected to do, he uses the power of the federal government to settle political scores.
**Minnesotans deserve better. So do working families everywhere.**
That’s why Small Town PAC is helping elect good leaders who will put their communities first, stand up to Trump’s bullying, and get to work solving problems instead of creating more chaos.

Tim

name: Ro Khanna
subject: Climate change is threatening our hospitals.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ro for Congress
body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
Americans and our institutions are vulnerable to the growing threat of climate change—and that includes our hospitals.
Climate change—including floods, heat waves, and wildfires—threatens the core of hospital care by damaging facilities and equipment. Recent events, such as the casualties during Hurricane Katrina, the loss of COVID-19 vaccines during the 2021 Texas ice storm, and the closure of Los Angeles hospitals during 2025 wildfires, underscore the urgent need for resilient medical infrastructure.
Meanwhile, the hospitals themselves are a major contributor to climate change. The healthcare sector is responsible for more than 8.5 percent of carbon emissions in the United States, more than a third of which come from hospitals. More people will suffer from environmental health issues as conditions worsen, creating a vicious cycle.
These problems cannot continue to be ignored. With the United States experiencing more than 20 major natural disasters per year, we must ensure that our medical facilities are prepared to respond.
https://x.com/EdMarkey/status/2082178694529888572 [https://x.com/EdMarkey/status/2082178694529888572]
Senator Ed Markey and I just reintroduced the Green New Deal for Health , legislation designed to meet this growing threat through initiatives that include:
✅ Improving hospital infrastructure by making it more resilient to natural disasters while reducing carbon emissions.
✅ Increasing support for home resiliency measures for medical needs by making solar batteries, heat pumps, and other resiliency measures eligible Medicare expenses, so people with disabilities and medical needs can install life-saving home infrastructure.
✅ Investing in frontline communities through climate and health education, a robust community health workforce, and hazard pay to workers who respond after a crisis.
✅ Establishing the National Climate and Health Research and Innovation Initiative to support research into the health impacts of climate change and develop innovative approaches to climate-health resilience.
Tell Congress: Pass the Green New Deal for Health. _" An appeaser is one who feeds a crocodile, hoping it will eat him last."_ Winston Churchill
The twentieth century offers a sobering record of political actors--revolutionaries, democrats, and statesmen alike--who mistook authoritarian movements for manageable partners. Whether inside a revolutionary coalition or across a diplomatic bargaining table, the pattern repeats: accommodation is offered in the name of stability, and the authoritarian faction accepts the concession not as a settlement but as a staging ground for further domination. Four documented cases--revolutionary Russia, Iran, Republican Spain, and interwar Britain-- trace the recurring miscalculations that enabled totalitarian forces to consolidate power.

"_One ought to remember that the history of mankind is a history of appeasement that didn 't work_." **[Dean Rusk](https://substack.com/redirect/82697882-8217-4515-afa2-9eebffe8fe15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (Former US Secretary of State)
The Democratic Party in the United States has historically functioned as a broad coalition, encompassing northern urban machines, southern conservatives, organized labor, civil rights advocates, and cosmopolitan professionals. The oldest active voter-based political party in the world being founded in 1828. Over the past three decades, however, the ideological center of gravity within that coalition has shifted in ways that have generated sustained intraparty tension. The center-left establishment associated with the presidencies of Bill Clinton and Barack Obama now competes for agenda-setting power with a progressive insurgency animated by Senator Bernie Sanders and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA)-aligned membership of Congress. The documented trajectory of that realignment, from the "New Democrat" ascendancy of the 1990s through the primary challenges and platform fights of the present era is notable.

* * *
Inflation isn't just prices going up. It's a symptom of a deeper breakdown -- in the four things money is supposed to hold together: effort, value, obligation, and time. When Congress lets those bonds dissolve, you don't just get poverty. You get a country that can no longer function as one.
In nearly 8 minutes, I walk through exactly how Congress has been breaking each of those bonds -- from the 17-year minimum wage freeze, to Wall Street gambling with your retirement, to the child tax credit they found, watched work, and let expire, to a Social Security shortfall they've known about for 30 years and never fixed.
This is not four separate problems. It's one problem showing up four times through a Congress that stopped representing the people a long time ago. History has a name for where this road leads. We're not there yet -- but you're feeling the erosion right now at the grocery store, the gas pump, and the kitchen table.
I'm Melissa Chaudhry, running for Congress in Washington's 9th District. Congress is making us broke. I'm running to fix it.

* * *
You work. You save. You try to be responsible.
Your paycheck is bigger than it was ten years ago. (Hopefully.) Your house, if you own one, shows a higher number. Your retirement account looks fatter.
And you feel poorer. Because you are.
Groceries cost more. Rent costs more. Insurance costs more. Childcare can swallow a paycheck whole. One medical bill can still wreck years of careful planning.
You are earning _**more dollars**_ that buy _**less life.**_
Most people are told that's just "inflation" -- a number, a statistic, a line on a chart that goes up. **It is not.**
It is the **visible symptom of something deeper breaking** , and once you see the deeper thing, you cannot unsee it.
* * *
Money makes four promises to a society that agrees to use that form of money.
1. It promises that **effort will be rewarded** -- work today, and your labor will command real value that you can use tomorrow.
2. It promises that **value will hold** -- save today, and what you set aside will still mean something later.
3. It promises that **obligations will be honored** -- borrow, lend, promise, and the terms will still be trustworthy when the bill comes due.
4. It promises that **time itself can be trusted** -- that a person can plan a life, plant an orchard, raise a child, buy a home, because tomorrow is not a stranger who owes you nothing.

**Effort. Value. Obligation. Time.**
Healthy money ties them together.
Break one of those promises and you have a policy problem. Break all four, slowly, for decades, while insisting nothing is wrong -- and you have something else. You have a country whose people no longer believe their own institutions, or that they can trust one another. And that is the beginning of a very dark time.
**A functioning society depends on** _**credible, consistent, reliable**_**relationships between** _**effort, value, obligation, and time**_**.**
This is the story of how, one broken promise at a time, ours started to buckle. And who let it happen.

## I. Effort -> Value: What Work Is Supposed to Buy
In 1971, the median new house in America cost about 2.4 years of a typical family's income. Today it costs at least 4, in some areas as much as 7. I live, as a renter, in one such area.
Houses are not sixteen times bigger, which is roughly how much more expensive they've become in raw dollars. A house does not require sixteen times the lumber, labor, and land it required in 1971. What changed is not the house. What changed is how much a year of your effort is worth against it.
Think of the economy as a pie. Houses, food, medicine, roads, factories, the labor of nurses and electricians and truck drivers -- that's what the real economy is made of. That's the pie. _Money is just a claim on a slice._ Print more claims and you do not bake more pie. You just cut it into smaller pieces and hand out more of them, and act surprised when everyone's slice shrinks.
More slices. Not more pie. More dollars - not more real economy.
Meanwhile, we have gotten dramatically better at actually making things. Better, faster, more efficient, cheaper tools, not to mention automation, shipping, computing -- American workers produce far more per hour than they did fifty years ago. If effort and value still meant what they're supposed to mean, that additional value created would show up in paychecks. It used to, for decades - the decades of the American middle class, when a single full-time worker could comfortably provide for a family of four with one income.
That stopped in the 70s. Productivity still went up, but wages didn't go up in proportion anymore. Virtually all of that wealth went somewhere else: to the corporations and their owners - millionaires and now billionaires who already owned owned the assets, the companies, the leverage.
Our society decided to reward _ownership_ over _labor_. **Extraction** over **production**.
That has consequences.
Here is the plainest evidence I can give you, and it is not a statistic economists argue about -- it is a fact anyone can check. **The federal minimum wage has been frozen at $7.25 an hour since July of 2009**. Seventeen years. That is the longest stretch without a single increase since the federal minimum wage was created in 1938. Not the longest in a while -- the longest _ever_. Congress raised it 22 times between 1938 and 2009. Then it simply stopped raising it, through recessions and recoveries, through a pandemic, through the highest inflation in forty years, while rent and groceries and childcare and tuition climbed without pause.
That is not an accident of the market. **That is a decision,** renewed every single session by our "Representatives," actively betraying us, who decline to make a different one.
And when Congress did finally, quietly acknowledge that money was flowing toward extraction instead of production -- when it passed a small tax on corporate stock buybacks in 2022 -- it set that tax at _**one percent**_. One penny on the dollar, on a practice that routes **hundreds of billions of dollars** a year away from wages, research, and hiring and into pushing up share prices for people who already hold the shares.
That is not a policy. That is a receipt. It's Congress telling you, in the smallest print available, that they know _exactly_ what's happening and have decided not to stop it.
This is effort losing its claim on value.
