## II. Value -> Time: What Saving Is Supposed to Protect
A retirement account is not supposed to be an abstraction. It is real decades of your actual labor, deferred -- money you didn't spend today because you trusted it would still mean something twenty years from now.
That trust is the entire premise of a pension, a 401(k), a savings account. **Value is supposed to survive the trip across time.**
Much of that deferred labor doesn't sit quietly in a vault, even though it probably should. It gets routed through the financial system -- pensions, retirement funds, bank deposits -- and loaned out, leveraged, and bet, often by people managing other people's money with very little of their own on the line. When the bets pay off, the gains are mostly private, routed to those managers. When the bets get big enough to threaten the whole system if they fail, the public is told the corporations involved are "too big to fail," and Congress makes the public absorb the loss instead.
_**Who decided to let them use our money to gamble with?
And then decided that they should be allowed to keep the winnings,
but if they lose big, it comes out of our pockets?**_
Privatized profits. Socialized losses. Most members of Congress can explain a defense appropriations bill in their sleep. Ask the same rooms to explain what a bank stress test actually protects, and watch how fast the conversation changes subject.
You do not have to take my word for the mechanism. You can watch it happen in real time.
In 2018, Congress passed a law rolling back bank oversight that had been put in place after 2008 -- specifically, raising the asset threshold at which a bank had to undergo mandatory stress testing from $50 billion to $250 billion. **It passed with support from both parties.**
It sounded, at the time, like a technical favor to smaller community banks. What it actually did was exempt dozens of large regional banks -- including one you may not have heard of before March of 2023, called Silicon Valley Bank -- from the very scrutiny that might have caught the risk building on their balance sheets before it became fatal.
When SVB collapsed with over $200 billion in assets, federal regulators stepped in over a weekend to guarantee deposits, including deposits far above the standard insurance limit, to stop the panic from spreading. The taxpaying public backstopped the failure. The lobbying that produced the exemption that led to the failure, had come from the banks themselves. And Congress went along with the banks.
That is quantitative easing's uglier cousin, playing out at the regulatory level instead of the monetary one: a system quietly rewritten, by the people's own "Representatives," to protect the institutions holding your money from the accountability that might have kept your money safer in the first place.
This is value losing its claim on time.

## III. Obligation -> Trust: What a Promise Is Supposed to Mean
Economic policy does not stay in DC. It permeates the whole economy, your bank account, your rental market, your paycheck and job opportunities. It even sidles into kitchens and bedrooms, where it can wreak havoc.
Suppose rent jumps 30 percent. Childcare eats a second paycheck. Groceries cost hundreds more a month. A car repair goes on a credit card charging more than 20 percent interest.
One partner starts working nights. The other carries more of the household. Both are exhausted. Every purchase becomes a negotiation. One person feels controlled. The other feels abandoned. Shame moves in. Resentment follows.
They may come to believe the other one caused the pain.
**But the pressure was built upstream, by people who will never sit at that kitchen table and never answer for what happened there.** DC can corrupt the love between two people simply by manipulating the conditions around money -- and the victims may never be able to trace where the damage actually came from.
_**That is one of the cruelest features of a broken promise in the structure of money. It leaves fingerprints everywhere and a signature nowhere.**_
The victims do not experience this change as an abstract decline in a purchasing-power index. **They experience it as betrayal.**
And sometimes obligation doesn't just erode quietly. Sometimes it gets broken on purpose, in writing, by people who face no real consequence for it.
For over a decade, employees at Wells Fargo opened more than three and a half million bank and credit card accounts in customers' names, without their knowledge or their consent. Forged signatures. Fake email addresses. Fees charged on accounts real people never asked for and never agreed to. That is not a clerical mistake. That is fraud, against the exact thing a contract is supposed to be: your agreement, your signature, your word.
The CEO who ran that bank the entire time it was happening, John Stumpf, walked away with a fine and a lifetime ban from banking. Not one day in prison. The bank clawed back some of his pay. That was the whole price, for millions of broken promises.
If a signature can be forged by a Fortune 500 bank for over a decade, and the answer is a fine the executive can absorb out of his own bonuses, then "obligation" stops meaning anything. Not for you. Not for anyone without a lobbyist.
Now, we know, with unusual clarity, what it looks like when this particular promise is **kept** instead of broken -- because we tried it, briefly, and then took it back. In 2021, Congress expanded the Child Tax Credit for one year: bigger payments, sent monthly, available to the families who needed it most. Child poverty fell from 9.7 percent to 5.2 percent -- the single largest one-year drop ever recorded, cutting it very nearly in half. Then the expansion was allowed to expire at the end of that year. Within months, more than 3.7 million children fell _back_ into poverty.
Congress did not fail to find a solution. **Congress found one, watched it work, and let it lapse anyway.**
That is what it means for obligation to lose its claim on trust: not that no one knew how to keep the promise, but that keeping it stopped being the priority the moment the cameras moved on.
That's not Representation of We the People. It's structural abandonment.

## IV. Time -> Future: What a Society Needs to Believe to Keep Building
Adam Fergusson's history of Germany's early-1920s hyperinflation, _When Money Dies,_ is not really a book about currency mechanics. It is a book about what happens to human beings when money stops carrying trustworthy information **across time.**
During that collapse, workers were sometimes paid daily and rushed to spend their wages before the next price increase. Often carrying their wages in a wheelbarrow, because the quantities involved had become astronomical. Savings vanished. Contracts stopped meaning anything. By the end, repricing was occurring by the hour, and barter and foreign currency had taken over. During the worst of it, in late 1923, a loaf of bread ran around **200 billion marks**. One year earlier, it had cost **163 marks**. And one year before that, it cost **4.**
Shortly thereafter, the government banned the central bank from printing more currency, and stepped in with a new currency unit tied to land values, then gold, which successfully restabilized the economy, though the transition was painful.
Argentina offers a quieter version of the same lesson across decades rather than months: repeated currency crises taught ordinary Argentines to distrust their own money so completely that they learned to convert wages into dollars immediately, shorten contracts, and brace for the next devaluation before it arrived. At one point, in 1989, the economy simply stopped functioning. Stores no longer stocked shelves because the price would change by the afternoon. President Alfonsin resigned five months early so his successor could step in.
But unlike in Germany, decades of effort have not fully yielded enduring improvements. Argentines today still, very often, in their own country, conduct business in a parallel "blue dollar" economy rather than in their own currency, because they don't believe in their own government's claim that the money has value.
America is not Weimar Germany, and it is not Argentina. But the underlying mechanism is universal, and it does not require hyperinflation to operate. **Money begins to die socially -- long before it dies technically -- the moment people stop believing it honestly connects the effort they make today with the security they were promised tomorrow.**
We are already watching that promise get tested at the most literal level there is: the one where you pay in for forty years and are told a number will be waiting for you when you stop working.
Social Security's retirement trust fund is now projected, in the government's own most recent report, to run out in late 2032 -- six years from now. If Congress does nothing between now and then, **retirees will face an automatic, across-the-board cut in benefits of roughly 20%.** This is not a surprise. Actuaries have been forecasting some version of this shortfall for more than thirty years.
Congress has held that knowledge the entire time and has not passed a permanent fix. There are several well-studied, ludicrously simple ways to solve this. Congress has chosen none of them.
Thirty years is not an oversight. Thirty years is a choice, made quietly, again and again, by people who will mostly not be the ones living on a reduced check.
**This is time losing its claim on the future.**

## V. The Collapse
None of these four breaks happens in isolation forever. Eventually they compound.
A government can degrade the promises underneath its currency for years before the public fully understands what has been taken. But once people stop believing that work will provide security, that saving will preserve value, and that institutions will honor what they promised, the crisis stops being merely economic.
It becomes social, moral, political, and **constitutional**.
People who are richer on paper and poorer in their actual command over life eventually understand that something has been taken from them. They may not know exactly what. They may blame their spouse, their neighbor, immigrants, "the economy," different religions, each other. That confusion is dangerous -- it lets the people who benefited from the arrangement redirect the anger somewhere else, letting us fight amongst ourselves while they walk away holding the bag.
**That is when economic mismanagement becomes civilizational danger.**
## VI. Nobody's Driving
Here is the pattern, laid end to end.
**Congress** let the wage floor freeze for seventeen years while productivity kept climbing. Allowing owners and capitalists, especially billionaires, to capture all of the gains in wealth, creating profoundly unfair and destabilizing inequality.
**Congress** deregulated bank oversight in 2018 and then bailed out the failure that followed in 2023 with public money.
**Congress** built a program in 2021 that cut child poverty nearly in half, watched it work, and let it die eleven months later.
**Congress** has known for three decades that Social Security's math doesn't add up, and that simple solutions remain available, and has not fixed it.
Four different decades. Four different excuses. One pattern: the people holding the **actual constitutional power to fix** each of these things -- the power of the purse, the power to legislate, the power that belongs to Congress and nowhere else in our government -- declined to use it.
Only Congress can do this. Only Congress can invest directly in the sectors that would actually restore what's been broken -- healthcare, housing supply, wages, care infrastructure, retirement security -- instead of just managing the financial symptoms of their absence. That is not a technical detail. That is the entire design of our government: **the power of the purse belongs to the people 's elected representatives precisely so that these choices get made in public,** by people who answer for them, instead of quietly, by whichever institution steps into the power vacuum Congress left.
For decades, Congress has abandoned the American people and abdicated their duty do that hard, accountable work -- because the hard work means confronting the donors, the industries, and the habits of extraction that benefit from things staying exactly as broken as they are.
**Effort. Value. Obligation. Time. And a monetary system that 's reliable enough to hold them together.**
Those are the four promises a functioning society has to keep. Right now, in DC, nobody is minding all four at once. Nobody is even trying.
It's time to send people to Congress who understand that the Federal Reserve was never supposed to be the only hand on the wheel -- and who are willing to step up as Representatives of the American People, and do the work of actually steering.
Care. Courage. The Constitution.

I do this work intensively, I care about it deeply, and I bring over 20 years ' experience to bear to provide maximum value to you. If you 're already a paid subscriber, thank you! You'll have automatic access to this. Everyone else - here 's our Election Week special: 20% off annual plans forever , for access into this deeper layer of my work. Closes Tuesday, August 4th, at midnight. If an annual plan is out of reach, don 't worry - any paid subscription level will get you access. I 'd love to see you there. You work. You save. You try to be responsible. Your paycheck is bigger than it was ten years ago. (Hopefully.) Your house, if you own one, shows a higher number. Your retirement account looks fatter. And you feel poorer. Because you are. Groceries cost more. Rent costs more. Insurance costs more. Childcare can swallow a paycheck whole. One medical bill can still wreck years of careful planning. You are earning more dollars that buy less life. Most people are told that's just "inflation" -- a number, a statistic, a line on a chart that goes up. It is not. It is the visible symptom of something deeper breaking , and once you see the deeper thing, you cannot unsee it. Money makes four promises to a society that agrees to use that form of money. 1. It promises that effort will be rewarded -- work today, and your labor will command real value that you can use tomorrow. 2. It promises that value will hold -- save today, and what you set aside will still mean something later. 3. It promises that obligations will be honored -- borrow, lend, promise, and the terms will still be trustworthy when the bill comes due. 4. It promises that time itself can be trusted -- that a person can plan a life, plant an orchard, raise a child, buy a home, because tomorrow is not a stranger who owes you nothing. Effort. Value. Obligation. Time. Healthy money ties them together. Break one of those promises and you have a policy problem. Break all four, slowly, for decades, while insisting nothing is wrong -- and you have something else. You have a country whose people no longer believe their own institutions, or that they can trust one another. And that is the beginning of a very dark time. A functioning society depends on credible, consistent, reliablerelationships between effort, value, obligation, and time. This is the story of how, one broken promise at a time, ours started to buckle. And who let it happen. I. Effort -> Value: What Work Is Supposed to Buy In 1971, the median new house in America cost about 2.4 years of a typical family's income. Today it costs at least 4, in some areas as much as 7. I live, as a renter, in one such area. Houses are not sixteen times bigger, which is roughly how much more expensive they've become in raw dollars. A house does not require sixteen times the lumber, labor, and land it required in 1971. What changed is not the house. What changed is how much a year of your effort is worth against it. Think of the economy as a pie. Houses, food, medicine, roads, factories, the labor of nurses and electricians and truck drivers -- that's what the real economy is made of. That's the pie. Money is just a claim on a slice. Print more claims and you do not bake more pie. You just cut it into smaller pieces and hand out more of them, and act surprised when everyone's slice shrinks. More slices. Not more pie. More dollars - not more real economy. Meanwhile, we have gotten dramatically better at actually making things. Better, faster, more efficient, cheaper tools, not to mention automation, shipping, computing -- American workers produce far more per hour than they did fifty years ago. If effort and value still meant what they're supposed to mean, that additional value created would show up in paychecks. It used to, for decades - the decades of the American middle class, when a single full-time worker could comfortably provide for a family of four with one income. That stopped in the 70s. Productivity still went up, but wages didn't go up in proportion anymore. Virtually all of that wealth went somewhere else: to the corporations and their owners - millionaires and now billionaires who already owned owned the assets, the companies, the leverage. Our society decided to reward ownership over labor. Extraction over production. That has consequences. Here is the plainest evidence I can give you, and it is not a statistic economists argue about -- it is a fact anyone can check. The federal minimum wage has been frozen at $7.25 an hour since July of 2009. Seventeen years. That is the longest stretch without a single increase since the federal minimum wage was created in 1938. Not the longest in a while -- the longest ever. Congress raised it 22 times between 1938 and 2009. Then it simply stopped raising it, through recessions and recoveries, through a pandemic, through the highest inflation in forty years, while rent and groceries and childcare and tuition climbed without pause. That is not an accident of the market. That is a decision, renewed every single session by our "Representatives," actively betraying us, who decline to make a different one. And when Congress did finally, quietly acknowledge that money was flowing toward extraction instead of production -- when it passed a small tax on corporate stock buybacks in 2022 -- it set that tax at one percent. One penny on the dollar, on a practice that routes hundreds of billions of dollars a year away from wages, research, and hiring and into pushing up share prices for people who already hold the shares. That is not a policy. That is a receipt. It's Congress telling you, in the smallest print available, that they know exactly what's happening and have decided not to stop it. This is effort losing its claim on value. II. Value -> Time: What Saving Is Supposed to Protect A retirement account is not supposed to be an abstraction. It is real decades of your actual labor, deferred -- money you didn't spend today because you trusted it would still mean something twenty years from now. That trust is the entire premise of a pension, a 401(k), a savings account. Value is supposed to survive the trip across time. Much of that deferred labor doesn't sit quietly in a vault, even though it probably should. It gets routed through the financial system -- pensions, retirement funds, bank deposits -- and loaned out, leveraged, and bet, often by people managing other people's money with very little of their own on the line. When the bets pay off, the gains are mostly private, routed to those managers. When the bets get big enough to threaten the whole system if they fail, the public is told the corporations involved are "too big to fail," and Congress makes the public absorb the loss instead. Who decided to let them use our money to gamble with? And then decided that they should be allowed to keep the winnings, but if they lose big, it comes out of our pockets? Privatized profits. Socialized losses. Most members of Congress can explain a defense appropriations bill in their sleep. Ask the same rooms to explain what a bank stress test actually protects, and watch how fast the conversation changes subject. You do not have to take my word for the mechanism. You can watch it happen in real time. In 2018, Congress passed a law rolling back bank oversight that had been put in place after 2008 -- specifically, raising the asset threshold at which a bank had to undergo mandatory stress testing from $50 billion to $250 billion. It passed with support from both parties. It sounded, at the time, like a technical favor to smaller community banks. What it actually did was exempt dozens of large regional banks -- including one you may not have heard of before March of 2023, called Silicon Valley Bank -- from the very scrutiny that might have caught the risk building on their balance sheets before it became fatal. When SVB collapsed with over $200 billion in assets, federal regulators stepped in over a weekend to guarantee deposits, including deposits far above the standard insurance limit, to stop the panic from spreading. The taxpaying public backstopped the failure. The lobbying that produced the exemption that led to the failure, had come from the banks themselves. And Congress went along with the banks. That is quantitative easing's uglier cousin, playing out at the regulatory level instead of the monetary one: a system quietly rewritten, by the people's own "Representatives," to protect the institutions holding your money from the accountability that might have kept your money safer in the first place. This is value losing its claim on time. III. Obligation -> Trust: What a Promise Is Supposed to Mean Economic policy does not stay in DC. It permeates the whole economy, your bank account, your rental market, your paycheck and job opportunities. It even sidles into kitchens and bedrooms, where it can wreak havoc. Suppose rent jumps 30 percent. Childcare eats a second paycheck. Groceries cost hundreds more a month. A car repair goes on a credit card charging more than 20 percent interest. One partner starts working nights. The other carries more of the household. Both are exhausted. Every purchase becomes a negotiation. One person feels controlled. The other feels abandoned. Shame moves in. Resentment follows. They may come to believe the other one caused the pain. But the pressure was built upstream, by people who will never sit at that kitchen table and never answer for what happened there. DC can corrupt the love between two people simply by manipulating the conditions around money -- and the victims may never be able to trace where the damage actually came from. That is one of the cruelest features of a broken promise in the structure of money. It leaves fingerprints everywhere and a signature nowhere. The victims do not experience this change as an abstract decline in a purchasing-power index. They experience it as betrayal. And sometimes obligation doesn't just erode quietly. Sometimes it gets broken on purpose, in writing, by people who face no real consequence for it. For over a decade, employees at Wells Fargo opened more than three and a half million bank and credit card accounts in customers' names, without their knowledge or their consent. Forged signatures. Fake email addresses. Fees charged on accounts real people never asked for and never agreed to. That is not a clerical mistake. That is fraud, against the exact thing a contract is supposed to be: your agreement, your signature, your word. The CEO who ran that bank the entire time it was happening, John Stumpf, walked away with a fine and a lifetime ban from banking. Not one day in prison. The bank clawed back some of his pay. That was the whole price, for millions of broken promises. If a signature can be forged by a Fortune 500 bank for over a decade, and the answer is a fine the executive can absorb out of his own bonuses, then "obligation" stops meaning anything. Not for you. Not for anyone without a lobbyist. Now, we know, with unusual clarity, what it looks like when this particular promise is kept instead of broken -- because we tried it, briefly, and then took it back. In 2021, Congress expanded the Child Tax Credit for one year: bigger payments, sent monthly, available to the families who needed it most. Child poverty fell from 9.7 percent to 5.2 percent -- the single largest one-year drop ever recorded, cutting it very nearly in half. Then the expansion was allowed to expire at the end of that year. Within months, more than 3.7 million children fell back into poverty. Congress did not fail to find a solution. Congress found one, watched it work, and let it lapse anyway. That is what it means for obligation to lose its claim on trust: not that no one knew how to keep the promise, but that keeping it stopped being the priority the moment the cameras moved on. That's not Representation of We the People. It's structural abandonment. IV. Time -> Future: What a Society Needs to Believe to Keep Building Adam Fergusson's history of Germany's early-1920s hyperinflation, When Money Dies, is not really a book about currency mechanics. It is a book about what happens to human beings when money stops carrying trustworthy information across time. During that collapse, workers were sometimes paid daily and rushed to spend their wages before the next price increase. Often carrying their wages in a wheelbarrow, because the quantities involved had become astronomical. Savings vanished. Contracts stopped meaning anything. By the end, repricing was occurring by the hour, and barter and foreign currency had taken over. During the worst of it, in late 1923, a loaf of bread ran around 200 billion marks. One year earlier, it had cost 163 marks. And one year before that, it cost 4. Shortly thereafter, the government banned the central bank from printing more currency, and stepped in with a new currency unit tied to land values, then gold, which successfully restabilized the economy, though the transition was painful. Argentina offers a quieter version of the same lesson across decades rather than months: repeated currency crises taught ordinary Argentines to distrust their own money so completely that they learned to convert wages into dollars immediately, shorten contracts, and brace for the next devaluation before it arrived. At one point, in 1989, the economy simply stopped functioning. Stores no longer stocked shelves because the price would change by the afternoon. President Alfonsin resigned five months early so his successor could step in. But unlike in Germany, decades of effort have not fully yielded enduring improvements. Argentines today still, very often, in their own country, conduct business in a parallel "blue dollar" economy rather than in their own currency, because they don't believe in their own government's claim that the money has value. America is not Weimar Germany, and it is not Argentina. But the underlying mechanism is universal, and it does not require hyperinflation to operate. Money begins to die socially -- long before it dies technically -- the moment people stop believing it honestly connects the effort they make today with the security they were promised tomorrow. We are already watching that promise get tested at the most literal level there is: the one where you pay in for forty years and are told a number will be waiting for you when you stop working. Social Security's retirement trust fund is now projected, in the government's own most recent report, to run out in late 2032 -- six years from now. If Congress does nothing between now and then, retirees will face an automatic, across-the-board cut in benefits of roughly 20%. This is not a surprise. Actuaries have been forecasting some version of this shortfall for more than thirty years. Congress has held that knowledge the entire time and has not passed a permanent fix. There are several well-studied, ludicrously simple ways to solve this. Congress has chosen none of them. Thirty years is not an oversight. Thirty years is a choice, made quietly, again and again, by people who will mostly not be the ones living on a reduced check. This is time losing its claim on the future. V. The Collapse None of these four breaks happens in isolation forever. Eventually they compound. A government can degrade the promises underneath its currency for years before the public fully understands what has been taken. But once people stop believing that work will provide security, that saving will preserve value, and that institutions will honor what they promised, the crisis stops being merely economic. It becomes social, moral, political, and constitutional. People who are richer on paper and poorer in their actual command over life eventually understand that something has been taken from them. They may not know exactly what. They may blame their spouse, their neighbor, immigrants, "the economy," different religions, each other. That confusion is dangerous -- it lets the people who benefited from the arrangement redirect the anger somewhere else, letting us fight amongst ourselves while they walk away holding the bag. That is when economic mismanagement becomes civilizational danger. VI. Nobody's Driving Here is the pattern, laid end to end. Congress let the wage floor freeze for seventeen years while productivity kept climbing. Allowing owners and capitalists, especially billionaires, to capture all of the gains in wealth, creating profoundly unfair and destabilizing inequality. Congress deregulated bank oversight in 2018 and then bailed out the failure that followed in 2023 with public money. Congress built a program in 2021 that cut child poverty nearly in half, watched it work, and let it die eleven months later. Congress has known for three decades that Social Security's math doesn't add up, and that simple solutions remain available, and has not fixed it. Four different decades. Four different excuses. One pattern: the people holding the actual constitutional power to fix each of these things -- the power of the purse, the power to legislate, the power that belongs to Congress and nowhere else in our government -- declined to use it. Only Congress can do this. Only Congress can invest directly in the sectors that would actually restore what's been broken -- healthcare, housing supply, wages, care infrastructure, retirement security -- instead of just managing the financial symptoms of their absence. That is not a technical detail. That is the entire design of our government: the power of the purse belongs to the people 's elected representatives precisely so that these choices get made in public, by people who answer for them, instead of quietly, by whichever institution steps into the power vacuum Congress left. For decades, Congress has abandoned the American people and abdicated their duty do that hard, accountable work -- because the hard work means confronting the donors, the industries, and the habits of extraction that benefit from things staying exactly as broken as they are. Effort. Value. Obligation. Time. And a monetary system that 's reliable enough to hold them together. Those are the four promises a functioning society has to keep. Right now, in DC, nobody is minding all four at once. Nobody is even trying. It's time to send people to Congress who understand that the Federal Reserve was never supposed to be the only hand on the wheel -- and who are willing to step up as Representatives of the American People, and do the work of actually steering. Care. Courage. The Constitution. | | ---|---|--- You 're currently a free subscriber to "It's a Matter of Integrity" by Melissa Chaudhry. clean_body: Trump is trying to rig the rules so his party cannot lose | | | Apparently, Donald Trump needs more reminders of a simple fact: he lost the 2020 election. He recently relitigated his defeat in a primetime presidential address, which was a rerun of previously debunked claims, undercut by the very same documents he released as “proof.” Americans see through the lies. Here in Georgia, we certainly know this playbook, because Trump and his allies ran it here first. And we know that his false claims of fraud are really about power — trying to control whose voices get heard, and whose get silenced: 1. Trump may have demanded that Georgia leaders “find 11,780 votes.” While they refused to commit treason, the next year they delivered laws to make it harder to vote by mail, register to vote and stay on the rolls, and have that vote counted. 2. Trump’s Department of Justice sent federal agents into the elections office in Fulton County, Georgia, and also went after election offices in Arizona and Michigan. 3. Now, Trump and his allies want to make their lies into federal law: new barriers between citizens and the ballot, aimed at the same voters who have always had to fight hardest to be heard. When they come for one of us — they are coming for all of us. A political party that cannot win a fair contest is trying to rig the rules so they cannot lose any more. = Authoritarians are trading democracy for cowardice. Patriots must exchange comfort for courage. Democracy is an action. It is the promise that we will share power even with those we disagree with, because that is the only way we secure a common future. Trump — and every extremist who stands with him — is asking us to give up our right to control our futures. His speech this month was a pretext: escalating an effort to manufacture a legal reason to do something drastic and alter the way the 2026 election is administered. That could mean declaring a national emergency to try to seize control over elections. It could also mean sending ICE or FBI agents to the polls to seize ballots or voting machines. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: This is an email about faith
body:
I’m asking you to have faith in me, Peter.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In just a minute, I’m going to personally ask you to **[make a $5 donation to my campaign for governor.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260801_1_leapoffaith.PDNcd5&refcode=em20260801-1721&amount=5&t=1&akid=1721%2E299639%2E-1qY9y)**
Before I do, I hope you’ll let me share **an important lesson I’ve learned about faith.**
Back in 2021, the Texas GOP was ramming an extreme anti-voter bill through the State House. The voter suppression bill they were pushing was ugly. It was dangerous. And I knew that staying put would mean letting Texans lose their freedom to vote.
So I took a leap of faith. I chose to walk off the floor.
But I knew I couldn’t stop this bill on my own. I needed my fellow Democratic legislators with me in order to break quorum. So I stood up, and I texted other legislators:
_“A leap of faith only works if you take it.”_
Together, we ran out the clock and stopped a bill designed to silence Texas voters. That quorum break protected Sunday morning voting — a sacred tradition in Black churches — and blocked a provision that would have allowed partisan judges to overturn election results without evidence. And we earned that victory together.
**Just like I needed my fellow Texas Democrats by my side on that day five years ago, I’m asking you to join me today.** I’m asking you to have faith that we can finally unseat corrupt Governor Greg Abbott and flip Texas together.
Each time you chip in to our people-powered campaign, you’re doing it alongside thousands of others who also believe in our power to win a brighter future for every Texan.
**[Can I count on you to donate to my grassroots campaign?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260801_1_leapoffaith.PDNcd5&refcode=em20260801-1721&amount=5&t=2&akid=1721%2E299639%2E-1qY9y)**

_A leap of faith only works if you take it._ And when you do, others will leap with you.
— Gina

subject: Every legal vote deserves to be protected
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Derek Schmidt for Congress, Inc
body:
Maintaining that confidence is a fundamental responsibility of the government.

| [](https://trk.emails.schmidt4congress._Lz9yZWN1cnJpbmc9dHJ1ZSZhbW91bnQ9MTAmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwODAxX1RJLUNDLjExMDExN190MTk3NDMzNy0zMjU5JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDgwMV9USS1DQy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NzQzMzctMzI1OSJ9/CrlM7SwY8A4_TGYu3w8Dvg)

Peter,When citizens step into the voting booth, they need full confidence that our election process is secure, accurate, and fair.Maintaining that confidence is a fundamental responsibility of the government.We recently saw what happens when administrative safeguards fail. In New Jersey, a software glitch improperly registered around 6,600 non-citizens on voter rolls. While officials work to clean up those records, it serves as a stark reminder of [why weak verification processes undermine public trust.](https://trk.emails.schmidt4congress._Lz9yZWN1cnJpbmc9dHJ1ZSZhbW91bnQ9MTAmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwODAxX1RJLUNDLjExMDExN190MTk3NDMzNy0zMjU5JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDgwMV9USS1DQy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NzQzMzctMzI1OSJ9/zE9xp6WCMr-9_HuYV062gA)During my time as Attorney General, I approached voter integrity with a simple principle: make it easy to vote and hard to cheat. Common-sense measures like proof of citizenship to register and valid photo ID at the ballot box protect the weight of every legal vote.Putting these protections in place takes sustained work. I rely on grassroots support from folks across Kansas to keep pushing for policies that protect our elections.[](https://trk.emails.schmidt4congress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTE1LjUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgwMV9USS1DQy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NzQzMzctMzI1OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MDFfVEktQ0MuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTc0MzM3LTMyNTkifQ/S3tVe5yS7IkrMOSQ1sFRnQ)[Would you consider pitching in $5 or $10 today to back our efforts?](https://trk.emails.schmidt4congress._Lz9yZWN1cnJpbmc9dHJ1ZSZhbW91bnQ9MTAmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwODAxX1RJLUNDLjExMDExN190MTk3NDMzNy0zMjU5JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDgwMV9USS1DQy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NzQzMzctMzI1OSJ9/cAsG33T-8C3vta2UdwRy5Q)

clean_body: Maintaining that confidence is a fundamental responsibility of the government. | Peter,When citizens step into the voting booth, they need full confidence that our election process is secure, accurate, and fair.Maintaining that confidence is a fundamental responsibility of the government.We recently saw what happens when administrative safeguards fail. In New Jersey, a software glitch improperly registered around 6,600 non-citizens on voter rolls. While officials work to clean up those records, it serves as a stark reminder of my time as Attorney General, I approached voter integrity with a simple principle: make it easy to vote and hard to cheat. Common-sense measures like proof of citizenship to register and valid photo ID at the ballot box protect the weight of every legal vote.Putting these protections in place takes sustained work. I rely on grassroots support from folks across Kansas to keep pushing for policies that protect our elections. | | Thank you for standing with me and for taking time to support our effort.Best,Derek Schmidt | Paid for by Derek Schmidt for Congress, Inc. 2. This legislation would also give Virginians the transparency you deserve. So that you know when a new data center is proposed to your community – and that these data centers can’t make secret deals with local governments and hide the details from you and your neighbors.

3. And I’m supporting the Power for the People Act, a bill that forces data centers to pay for the grid upgrades they require, instead of you. body:
Help us do what we do best.
#
Peter,
Donating to Voto Latino is the most direct ways to grow Latino voter participation in the elections that will decide our future.
[**If you’re ready to power our voter registration work from now til November, chip in $3 or any amount today.**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/531?c0=em-ms-voto-20260801-1.PkSSfE&refcode=em20260801-439&t=1&akid=439%2E1366028%2EGFNAXX)
Here are three powerful reasons why you should make an investment in Voto Latino today:
**1\. We know how to register Latino voters.**
**We’ve helped millions of people navigate the voting process** , from registering and checking status to finding polling locations and making a plan to vote. Registering voters is how we fight back against Trump and his allies’ anti-voter stunts, because the more of us who are on the rolls and ready to vote, the harder it is for them to silence us.

**2\. Our work has a proven track record.**
**Since 2004, we’ve registered nearly 2 million voters.** In 2020 alone, we registered more than **650,000 voters** , and **82% of those voters turned out.** Since 2012, we’ve registered **334,484 voters in battleground states** where elections are often decided by razor-thin margins.

**3\. The work is urgent, and the gap is still real**
Millions of eligible Latino voters are still unregistered. With the midterms just **14 weeks away and _even less time_ before voter registration deadlines,** closing that gap now means more people informed, registered, and ready to show up when it counts. Because we know that in race after race this November, Latinos will be the margin of victory.
**If these three reasons convinced you:**
**[Will you give $3 today to help Voto Latino register more voters ahead of November 3rd and strengthen Latino political power?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/531?c0=em-ms-voto-20260801-1.PkSSfE&refcode=em20260801-439&t=2&akid=439%2E1366028%2EGFNAXX)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

* * *
Radical DEI initiatives have been hollowing out some of America's most powerful and influential institutions for years. The American Bar Association has become a victim of diversity, equity, and inclusion standards that have severely impacted their judicial ethics.
The Defending Constitutional Rights and Exposing Institutional Task Force is a new House Oversight group committed to cracking down on DEI, welfare abuse, and free speech issues. In one of their first hearings last week, Chairman Brandon Gill **[stated](https://substack.com/redirect/2fbeee7e-a571-41f3-bfc1-4a94441cb83e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that "The ABA--an organization made up of attorneys who should know better--persisted in promoting DEI practices even though race-based admissions, forced speech, and considering race in employment decisions clearly violate the law."
[| | | | | Brandon Gill
---
@realBrandonGill
I spent two minutes asking the American Bar Association's President if race should be considered in law school admissions decisions. She refused to give a definitive answer.
| 8:17 PM * Jul 22, 2026 * 282K Views674 Replies * 4.38K Reposts * 21.5K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/7ceec0d3-b565-496b-bda9-1df3beb343ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The American Bar association plays a key role in the U.S. justice system as the only accreditor of American law schools. This means that it has the sole power to influence the entire U.S. legal system, from determining education requirements to evaluating judicial nominees. Their radicalization has severe, dangerous consequences for the integrity of the law.
Between 2017-2018, the ABA began implementing **[Standard 206](https://substack.com/redirect/efc2b91d-45b1-4233-bfcb-fa6d13f6c25d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , which required law schools to enact concrete plans to "commit to diversity," and to provide entry "into the profession by members of underrepresented groups, particularly racial and ethnic minorities." In the 2023 cases _Students for Fair Admissions, Inc. v. President & Fellows of Harvard College_ and _Students for Fair Admissions, Inc. v. University of North Carolina,_ the Supreme Court ruled that race-based admissions processes were a violation of federal law. In defiance of SCOTUS, the ABA sought to find workarounds. Rep. Gill stated that the ABA believed "_illegality is ... not a justification for a school's noncompliance with Standard 206."_
Additionally, the ABA pushed **[Standard 303(C)](https://substack.com/redirect/712ea0ce-5358-4f4f-a0b6-21587aaff80c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , which required law schools to teach courses on "bias, cross-cultural competency, and racism." The purpose of the courses were allegedly to "eliminate racism in the legal profession." In compliance, the **[University of Buffalo](https://substack.com/redirect/fa35ef24-2d1d-4de9-8196-ee74ec528459?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** taught courses that emphasized figures like George Floyd and Breonna Taylor. Students were required to read articles like "Securitizing Gender in the War on Terror and Crime" and watch videos titled "What is systemic racism?" and "How to Be a Good Ally- Identity, Privilege, Resistance." The course concluded with a "call to action," that vaguely alludes to racial activism.
Despite federal pressure, the ABA has not backed down on its DEI initiatives. In February 2026, ABA President Michelle Behnke claimed that organization would "not abandon our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion." Their website has a major section devoted to diversity, including an award for "**[Excellence in Pipeline Diversity.](https://substack.com/redirect/ab9673f7-e05d-446d-98d2-dc4360c0cf1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** " The Award specifically intends to "increase diversity in the legal profession."
In a written testimony, Zack Smith, a Senior Legal Fellow at The Heritage Foundation claimed that the ABA is a "partisan program full of radical policies." Smith pointed out that the ABA has a long history of punishing law schools who refused to comply with a race-based admissions process. The ABA repeatedly **[threatened](https://substack.com/redirect/7f26e461-baa3-4b4d-abf9-e16c59e3a1a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to pull accreditation from George Mason University Law School for not implementing racial quotas.
In September 2025, the ABA once again tried to pull accreditation, this time from St. Thomas University for not meeting racial requirements. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier stated that "The ABA may dislike Christian values, but it can't withhold accreditation to coerce schools to adopt its repugnant policies." This further proved that the ABA was more than willing to bully schools who didn't accept affirmative action measures.
[| | | | | Attorney General James Uthmeier
---
@AGJamesUthmeier
The American Bar Association recently suggested that St. Thomas University College of Law was not in compliance due to the school's Christian values. The ABA may dislike Christian values, but it cannot withhold accreditation to coerce schools to adopt its repugnant policies.
| 4:50 PM * Nov 6, 2025 * 282K Views172 Replies * 1.59K Reposts * 5.91K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/94cb89e0-8593-40d6-94fd-537125dee53b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A former student at Penn Law **[testified](https://substack.com/redirect/329f152f-8d35-442a-93e5-a02ded36536a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that the school operated as a "closed ideological loop; one that mandates conformity to Critical Race Theory (CRT), coerces student speech, and actively censors dissenting viewpoints." In detailing his experiences, he spoke about how professors prioritized critical race theorists and presented "radical critiques of law enforcement and the American justice system." In an assignment, he was forced to write an essay on systemic racism, and the grading rubric was influenced by how well students accepted the course's racial justice framing.
The ABA being politically compromised is alarming and consequential. It is the gatekeeper to those intending to learn and wield American law - a practice that begets sustained societal outcomes that affect our country greatly and often permanently.

In one of their first hearings last week, Chairman Brandon Gill that "The ABA--an organization made up of attorneys who should know better--persisted in promoting DEI practices even though race-based admissions, forced speech, and considering race in employment decisions clearly violate the law." The American Bar association plays a key role in the U.S. justice system as the only accreditor of American law schools. This means that it has the sole power to influence the entire U.S. legal system, from determining education requirements to evaluating judicial nominees. Their radicalization has severe, dangerous consequences for the integrity of the law. Between 2017-2018, the ABA began implementing , which required law schools to enact concrete plans to "commit to diversity," and to provide entry "into the profession by members of underrepresented groups, particularly racial and ethnic minorities." In the 2023 cases Students for Fair Admissions, Inc. v. President & Fellows of Harvard College and Students for Fair Admissions, Inc. v. University of North Carolina, the Supreme Court ruled that race-based admissions processes were a violation of federal law. In defiance of SCOTUS, the ABA sought to find workarounds. Rep. Gill stated that the ABA believed "illegality is ... not a justification for a school's noncompliance with Standard 206." | Letter from the Chair
---
One Vote Away from the Abyss: How Our Institutions Have Turned Socialistic and Propagandized
Fellow Republicans,
Look around. The institutions that once safeguarded liberty, truth, and the American way of life are no longer neutral referees. They have been steadily captured by democrat socialistic impulses and relentless propaganda. The evidence is daily, undeniable, and accelerating. And the hard truth is this: we are one vote--one election, one Senate seat, one Supreme Court appointment--away from descending even further into a system that prioritizes control over freedom, ideology over parents, and open borders over citizens.
The Media's Propaganda Machine
We observe it every single day. Mainstream media no longer reports news; it curates narratives. Anthony Fauci's recent congressional testimony and the admissions buried in his own government journals were largely ignored--except when outlets rushed to defend him. The same blackout greeted the recently released Biden tapes. When inconvenient facts threaten the preferred storyline, they simply vanish from the front page. This is not journalism. It is institutional propaganda designed to shield progressive orthodoxy and keep the public in the dark.
Nationalized Healthcare's Broken Promise
Socialism's track record on healthcare is on full display for anyone willing to look. During the recent FIFA matches, Canadians appeared in clips explaining why they crossed into the United States for care. They spoke of crushing waits and rationing back home, contrasted with the efficiency of American treatment--"get in and get out." These are not anecdotes from the distant past. They are live warnings of what government-run medicine delivers: delayed care, higher ultimate costs, and the quiet erosion of individual choice. Expanding that model here would not be compassion. It would be surrender.
Open Borders and the Erosion of Sovereignty
Just days ago, we watched masses of illegal immigrants come ashore off the coast of Spain, flooding towns and entering homes. The scenes were familiar because our own southern border towns lived them not long ago. Open borders are not humanitarian policy; they are the deliberate abandonment of national sovereignty. When institutions treat illegal entry as a right rather than a crime, they import instability, strain public resources, and signal that the rules no longer apply to those who follow them. A nation that cannot control its borders will not long control its destiny.
The Suppression of Faith
Remember the grandmothers. Under the Biden administration, elderly women praying peacefully outside abortion facilities were prosecuted and locked up. Biden's DOJ issued a memorandum listing Catholic churches as a threat and surveilled them.
The message was clear: certain forms of religious expression, especially those that challenge progressive sacred cows, will be treated as threats. When the state weaponizes law against quiet prayer, it is not defending rights--it is suppressing the moral foundations that once undergirded our culture. Faith is not optional window dressing in a free society. It is a bulwark against the soft tyranny of the administrative state.
The Assault on the Family and the Next Generation
Perhaps the most insidious advance of this socialistic mindset is the systematic undermining of the family. Schools increasingly indoctrinate rather than educate. Parental influence is treated as an obstacle. Christianity is scrubbed from classrooms while gender confusion is elevated as settled truth. The results speak for themselves: dismal proficiency scores, confused children, and a generation taught to distrust the very parents who love them. When institutions replace the family as the primary authority over children, they are not advancing progress--they are engineering dependency and division.
These are not isolated failures. They form a pattern: media that propagandizes, healthcare that nationalizes, borders that dissolve, faith that is punished, and families that are sidelined. Each step moves us closer to a society in which the individual serves the collective, and dissent is pathologized.
The conclusion is inescapable. We are one vote away from locking these trends into permanent power. The remedy is not despair or resignation. It is clarity, courage, and action at the ballot box and beyond. Support Republican candidates who will restore institutional neutrality, secure the border, defend parental rights, protect religious liberty, and reject the siren song of socialism. Speak the truth without apology. Demand accountability from every media outlet, school board, and agency that has forgotten its proper role.
America's institutions can still be reclaimed. But only if we refuse to look away--and only if we vote as if the future of the republic depends on it. Because it does.
Together, We Win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

Peter,

If you've ever had a kid, know someone with kids, or spent any time in a classroom, you know August is a strange month.

For educators, it's lesson plans and making sure everything is ready before students walk through the door. For parents, it's shopping for school supplies and doing everything possible to convince your kids that waking up before 10 a.m. isn't actually cruel (okay, it is). As a family, you're trying to squeeze every last bit of fun out of summer while the days count down way too fast.

It's the month where you're wrapping one chapter up while racing to get ready for the next. Campaigns aren't all that different.

August is the bridge between our summer organizing and the hardest stretch of this race. The work we do over the next few weeks will determine how prepared we'll be when Election Day starts coming into view.

That's why I'm so excited to tell you we started August with some great news: **thanks to this incredible team, we reached our $15,000 end-of-month fundraising goal. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.**

I know you have a busy life. The fact that you choose to spend even a few minutes reading these emails or making a contribution means more to me than I can say.

Thank you,

Christina Bohannan

Christina Bohannan is a mom, law professor, engineer and former state representative. She's running for Congress to defeat Mariannette Miller-Meeks and flip IA-01 blue.

The first month of the general election is officially over, and I wanted to sincerely thank you for your support as a key member of this movement. Here’s what you helped us accomplish in July: We only have three months left until November 3rd. That’s less than a hundred days away, and my team and I plan to make the most of every single hour. We’re going to keep criss-crossing the state, speaking with voters everywhere, and making our plan to win. I’m committed to being a governor who _truly listens_ to you — and that’s why I wanted to share a quick note on the survey we sent around a few weeks ago. If you received our survey, you might remember that I promised you I’d read every response. To show you I kept that promise, here are a few takeaways from what you shared with me:
* The top issue was **protections for our air, land, and water.** A full 76% of you chose this one, and I understand why. As the climate crisis is driving the risk of wildfires and creating a serious drought, this issue touches our daily lives and is impossible to ignore. That’s why, as your next governor, I’m prepared to fight for the only planet we have while still keeping costs down.
* The next two most popular issues were **standing up to Trump**(74% chose this one) and **our rights and freedoms**(67% picked this one). I agree wholeheartedly that these challenges are urgent, and I see how connected they are. As your governor, I look forward to taking more opportunities to be the fighter our state needs.
* 211 folks used the open-ended text box to let us know what other issues were on their minds. They uplifted issues like affordability, immigrant rights, and eliminating dark money from our elections. These are all concerns I share and will be ready to take action on as your next governor.

**[If you missed your chance earlier to take the survey, I’d still appreciate hearing your opinions! Please make your voice heard by clicking right here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136436645/637448941/-149875897?refcode=ea.0b9f740d-c28d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.0b9f740d-c28d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYjlmNzQwZC1jMjhkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Ry1ZIAzY4-AZCx5Bkn5vKN4QIDQYJ0LTuExUc3dQd2c=&emci=ed90b4de-0b8d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=0b9f740d-c28d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=51844520)** See you out on the campaign trail. my friend, it's been a while since I've written, and I wanted to fix that.
You signed up to follow our work here in Durham, and lately I've been too quiet in your inbox. So I'm writing to say thank you, and to fill you in on what we've been up to!
The state still isn't fully funding our public schools, and now the federal government is cutting the dollars our kids depend on. So Durham stepped up this year. When our classified school staff, the bus drivers, custodians and teacher assistants who keep our schools running, asked for a real raise, I pushed hard for it. We didn't get all the way there, but we made progress, and I'm not stopping until it's a true living wage!
That's what I care about most: our schools and the people who hold this county together. Everyone should be able to live with dignity, especially in Durham.
We start to build a brighter future when we show up in little ways, where we can. I'm proud of how we show up for our neighbors and know our future is limitless as long as we continue to care for each other.
If you want to see how these decisions are made, I put together a place that breaks it down so you can stay informed:

Thank you for being part of this movement,
Peter.

Our movement doesn't run on corporate
PACs or dark money. It runs on people like you — showing up when you can,
however you can, because you know it makes a difference.

And it all adds up, but right now, our collective power is being tested.
Two of our champions, Rashida and Ilhan, are facing primaries this month,
with outside forces and corporate-backed money lining up to try to knock
them out.

It's the same playbook every time — outspend, overwhelm, hope grassroots
supporters don't show up.

But we've seen what happens when people take a stand instead. Thousands of
supporters coming together, believing in something bigger than themselves
— that's how the Squad keeps winning. That's how our champions stay in
Congress fighting for affordable healthcare, workers' rights, real climate
action, and justice.

The Squad Victory Fund exists to protect and defend that fight, seat by
seat. But we can't do it alone, and we were never supposed to. This has
always been about all of us, together.

So thank you — for showing up and being part of something built by the
people. With the strength of this movement, we can keep winning, time and
time again.

— Squad Victory HQ

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are taking a stand against Trump,
his MAGA cronies, and anyone who stands in the way of justice — but they

Friend, My nickname in Congress is “Mama Bear” because I never back down from bullies and corporations that try to hurt our communities and profit off our pain. I’m running for re-election to keep fighting in Congress to protect you and your family. For example, here are recent policies I’ve introduced to protect you from lead poisoning, data centers, corporate price-gouging, and economic abuse:
* The __**_No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act_** __ would permanently ban large AI data centers and related infrastructure on land owned or managed by the U.S. government. Our public lands are for us, not destructive and polluting data centers!
* The **_GET THE LEAD OUT Act_** and the **_Removing Existing Pipes with Lead and Advancing Clean Environments (REPLACE) Act_** , which I’m co-leading with Rep. Shontel Brown,**** would address the lead poisoning crisis by removing lead from drinking water and from our homes.
* The******_FAIR Credit Act_** _(Fostering Accuracy and Integrity in the Reporting of Credit)_ would restore credit for victims of predatory lending, fraud, and financial abuse — and ban medical debt from being included on credit reports. This expands opportunities for Americans whose credit scores have blocked them from accessing basic needs like housing.
* The** _Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act_** would prohibit stores from using cameras and your personal data to manipulate and raise food prices.

Thank you for taking action! It’s an honor to work for you in Congress.
My first bill signed into law was the **_Payee Fraud Prevention Act_** _,_ to stop fraudulent activity that targets seniors, retirees, and people with disabilities. **The**** _Housing Our Communities Act_** was my latest bill to become law — it will fund affordable housing across the country and bring us closer to ensuring safe, affordable housing as a human right for all.
I also created the nation’s first water assistance and shutoff prevention program, **securing over $1.1 billion to stop water shutoffs** for people who can’t afford rising water bills, and I’ve introduced the **_Water Access & Affordability Act _**to create the first permanent federal water affordability program.
And I passed the **_Restoring Communities Left Behind Act_** , which funds home repairs and neighborhood revitalization. Since I began in Congress in 2019, I’ve also **brought home $68 million for projects across every community in my congressional district** , including over $7 million for home repair programs for seniors and flood victims, and over $20 million to remove and replace lead pipes and improve infrastructure.
I’ve also worked with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to change the lives of 15 million Americans by **removing $50 billion in medical debt from their credit reports**. Trump undid this progress but our fight is not over!
In Congress, **I serve on the House Oversight Committee & Financial Services Committee **where I fight against Big Banks, the Trump administration, and corporations that profit off our pain.
I’ve also co-founded and I co-lead the **Get The Lead Out Caucus** and the **People’s Environmental Justice Caucus** in Congress,**** to build on the work we’ve started to guarantee everyone the right to drink clean water, breathe clean air, and live in a healthy environment.
And I’m supporting and leading legislation to put a nationwide moratorium on data centers’ expansion, erase medical debt and utility debt (including water bills), guarantee healthcare for all Americans, hold utilities and other for-profit corporations accountable, and end poverty.
I’m running for Congress again because I know we have more work to do together. And I’m grateful to be with you in the fight for a democracy and economy where we can all thrive.
Always serving you,
Rashida

clean_body: I’m fighting in Congress to protect you and your family, including introducing recent policies to protect you from lead poisoning, data centers, corporate price-gouging, and financial abuse. | | | Friend, My nickname in Congress is “Mama Bear” because I never back down from bullies and corporations that try to hurt our communities and profit off our pain. I’m running for re-election to keep fighting in Congress to protect you and your family. For example, here are recent policies I’ve introduced to protect you from lead poisoning, data centers, corporate price-gouging, and economic abuse: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would permanently ban large AI data centers and related infrastructure on land owned or managed by the U.S. government. Our public lands are for us, not destructive and polluting data centers! The GET THE LEAD OUT Act and the Removing Existing Pipes with Lead and Advancing Clean Environments (REPLACE) Act , which I’m co-leading with Rep. Shontel Brown,** would address the lead poisoning crisis by removing lead from drinking water and from our homes. The****FAIR Credit Act (Fostering Accuracy and Integrity in the Reporting of Credit) would restore credit for victims of predatory lending, fraud, and financial abuse — and ban medical debt from being included on credit reports. This expands opportunities for Americans whose credit scores have blocked them from accessing basic needs like housing. The Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act would prohibit stores from using cameras and your personal data to manipulate and raise food prices. | Thank you for taking action! It’s an honor to work for you in Congress. My first bill signed into law was the Payee Fraud Prevention Act , to stop fraudulent activity that targets seniors, retirees, and people with disabilities. The** Housing Our Communities Act was my latest bill to become law — it will fund affordable housing across the country and bring us closer to ensuring safe, affordable housing as a human right for all. I also created the nation’s first water assistance and shutoff prevention program, securing over $1.1 billion to stop water shutoffs for people who can’t afford rising water bills, and I’ve introduced the Water Access & Affordability Act to create the first permanent federal water affordability program. And I passed the Restoring Communities Left Behind Act , which funds home repairs and neighborhood revitalization. Since I began in Congress in 2019, I’ve also brought home $68 million for projects across every community in my congressional district , including over $7 million for home repair programs for seniors and flood victims, and over $20 million to remove and replace lead pipes and improve infrastructure. I’ve also worked with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to change the lives of 15 million Americans by removing $50 billion in medical debt from their credit reports. Trump undid this progress but our fight is not over! In Congress, I serve on the House Oversight Committee & Financial Services Committee where I fight against Big Banks, the Trump administration, and corporations that profit off our pain. I’ve also co-founded and I co-lead the Get The Lead Out Caucus and the People’s Environmental Justice Caucus in Congress,** to build on the work we’ve started to guarantee everyone the right to drink clean water, breathe clean air, and live in a healthy environment. And I’m supporting and leading legislation to put a nationwide moratorium on data centers’ expansion, erase medical debt and utility debt (including water bills), guarantee healthcare for all Americans, hold utilities and other for-profit corporations accountable, and end poverty. I’m running for Congress again because I know we have more work to do together. And I’m grateful to be with you in the fight for a democracy and economy where we can all thrive. Fellow Patriot,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. Trump is stacking the
federal bench with cronies, loyalists, and political puppets — judges
whose real job isn't to interpret the law. It's to protect him.

And 19 Senate Democrats are letting him get away with it.

We've seen what that's cost us: the chaos, the rollback of our rights, the
siding with billionaires and corporations while everyone else gets left
behind.

Champions:

* Champions who don't vote yes on Trump’s corrupt nominees just because
leadership tells them to fall in line.
* Champions who won't return blue slips and roll out the red carpet for
Trump's court takeover.
* Champions who don't preach resistance in public and then hand Trump a
lifetime appointment to the bench.

actually do it — when it's hard, when it's inconvenient, when it matters
most.

Help us replace a Do-Nothing Democrat with a champion for working people.
#
**Tuesday is the day, Peter: it’s the Democratic primary election in Michigan** , where we can unseat a shameless and self-serving incumbent, Rep. Shri Thanedar.
Our candidate, Donavan McKinney, is facing off against this Do-Nothing Democrat to give the people of the Mighty 13th District a real fighter in Washington. **[He needs us now more than ever: rush $10 or more now to help him win!](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260801-1-dm.Po8wpQ&refcode=em20260801-38114&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=38114%2E1203867%2EdrG-4L)**
Shri is a self-funding multimillionaire who bought his way into Congress the first time around. Then, when he ran for re-election, he was propped up by millions of dollars in support from AIPAC and corporate super PACs.
This time, **AIPAC and its network of Republican megadonors, the Crypto lobby, and corporations like Detroit utility monopoly DTE are flooding this race** to try and save his seat.
Shri told his constituents he doesn’t take any money from corporate PACs or billionaires: _he lied._
Progressive and democratic socialist Donavan McKinney is the only candidate in this race who rejects corporate PAC money, because he’s truly committed to the people of Detroit.
**Corporations like DTE and billionaires backing Shri are doing so because they know in Congress, he fights for them — not us.** It’s time we replace Shri this Tuesday with a true champion for working people who will fight to lower costs, increase wages, stop funding genocide, abolish ICE, and pass Medicare for All.

Mike Rogers has an ad out, where he's wearing one of those tech-guy fleece vests, strolling through a factory, posing next to a drill press, and drinking a beer in a bar. Because I guess all of that is supposed to say _I 'm a working Michigander_?
You may remember his previous ad, where he wore a brand-new Carhartt jacket and pretended to be an expert in Michigan manufacturing. Well, now it's the fleece vest, and he's pretending to be middle class. The ad even says that's "who we are."
Respectfully, I disagree.
Let me tell you who Mike Rogers is: **Mike Rogers is a super-rich Florida man with a giant waterfront mansion.** In the winter, when Michiganders are scraping ice off their windshields in the cold, Mike Rogers is enjoying the palm trees at his mansion in Cape Coral and his two luxury yachts. (No joke, Google it.)
That's Mike Rogers. There's nothing wrong with relaxing on the beach, but there's something deeply wrong with being a carpetbagger millionaire who films himself at a factory and tells Michigan he's one of us.
Rogers doesn't know anything about Michigan grit. Most Florida millionaires don't.
But I know who we are. The Michigan way is folks busting their tails - it's calloused hands, shop floors, union halls. It's pride. It's building things that last. It's standing up for your neighbor. It's having the backs of your fellow workers. It's about looking out for community. It's not about hightailing it to your Florida mansion.
**So here 's what I want to say to Mike Rogers directly: Standing next to a drill press doesn't make you a fighter for the people who run it. Chatting with workers for a camera crew before flying home to Florida is not the same as working like hell to keep their factory open. And having a beer with some folks in a Michigan bar doesn't change your values. It doesn't suddenly give you credit. Working families shouldn't trust you, despite your (literal) costume changes.**
I've actually done the work. I served as Chief of Staff on President Obama's auto rescue when the whole world was ready to write off Michigan, and we helped save 200,000 jobs here. I helped write and pass the CHIPS and Science Act to bring manufacturing back to American soil, and to Michigan.
I didn't stop to shoot a commercial to make sure everybody saw how working-class I was. I was too busy busting my tail for the people who actually run those factories.
So let's be honest about what Mike Rogers would actually do for Michigan's working families: exactly what Donald Trump has done. That's who he answers to. Trump endorsed him (twice), MAGA billionaires fund him, and if he ever made it to the Senate, he'd vote however they tell him to. Rogers doesn't care if your grocery bill goes up, if gas prices skyrocket again, or if you lose your health insurance. _He cares about looking like he cares._
This ad just started running, and there is a heap of money behind it. Last cycle, Mike Rogers had $82.3 million in ad support from Republicans for his Senate campaign. He lost anyway, because Michiganders know B.S. when they see it.
But the out-of-state far-right billionaires funding him are going to run it back, bigger. The fleece vest is going to be in your living room, on your phone, and in the middle of your Tigers games - then your Lions and Red Wings and Pistons games - from now until November.
It's going to be exhausting.
So here's the plainest thing I can tell you about how we fight back: **We keep our TV ads on the air.**
Their MAGA Trump consultants think a guy who walks around factories talking about being middle class is going to win votes here. They think Michiganders can't tell the difference. But Rogers is a fake. He wouldn't know the Michigan way if it bit him on the keester.
Our ads tell the truth: about my record, about fighting for working families, about who actually shows up for Michigan. Keeping them running is the single most strategic thing this campaign can do right now, and I truly can't do it without you.
So if you're able, **[will you chip in today, drown out Mike Rogers ' ads, and help us keep telling Michiganders the truth before the primary in three days?](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e14216-7fbe-4f49-a327-215684d9586f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
We have to win this primary, beat Mike Rogers, flip the Senate, and stop Donald Trump - and all of it starts with fighting back against this ad. It's simple, but it's true. That's where your $20 donation goes. Telling the world who Mike Rogers really is.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e14216-7fbe-4f49-a327-215684d9586f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Mike Rogers can keep the vest. He can keep the Florida mansion and the luxury yachts, too.
But Michigan is ours.
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
